name: Phil Dalencour
text:
The front staff here particularly Luis is really great. He's been very informative and helpful for everything we've needed and every issue we've needed including changing rooms which was a non issue.

The pool and hot tub are both solid with the worst part of each being the chairs which are badly rusted or dirty however setting up your towels on the side of the pool deck is just fine and there's more than enough room for it. There's great restaurants about 7 minutes away in Barre downtown and past a wonderful drive about 13 minutes away in Montpelier. Seriously do that drive, it's beautiful.

The rooms in the 300s are solid. Lots of room, balcony, double double beds and a pull out couch and most importantly, two window exposures on both sides of the room. The other rooms without that are challenged since you either have to open the window into the public view or it's dark. This impacts the low 100s much more than the second floor and 300 rooms or those rooms above the check-in main building. Some issues with there being no smoking section so everywhere tends to have a lace of smoke in it but keeping the AC on typically helps with that - (unless your room is in front of smoker spots in which case the AC filters but still sends in smokey smelling air), and clearing out any humidity/dank smells in the summer heat. The smoke and dark room thing happened to us and switching rooms to the 300s fixed all of that.

The facilities outside of the rooms are always very clean and well kept though there is a crazy fruit fly issue. They aren't that bothersome though. All in all, a good place for the price, great front desk staff, particularly Luis, and a fun pool hot tub deck area, with big rooms

name: Mary Cain
text:
Difficult to find from Berlin exit at night. Easy on line reservations. Friendly check in staff. Getting to room was scary. First open at first floor parking to a hallway with 2 connecting doors. It was dark.

Room was FREEZING COLD with the window wide open! At 9pm at night which was below street level so anyone could have been inside waiting.  Clerk claimed that the housekeepers must have done that. Uncomfortable and got a chill waiting for heater to warm up.

Getting to the bathroom was soo tight I could barely get to it as the door was too close to the seating  chair AND the sink was overextended into the doorway! The tub stopper didn't work and all I wanted was to soak after a very long day.

TV worked-nice size fridge-nice closet space. Nice decor. Nice mattress. Getting to breakfast was also dangerous. Steep stairs-very dark underground basement. No attendant. Traditional breakfast and waffle self serve.

No receipt upon checkout claiming they couldn't give a receipt as it was made on line.I requested one. Really? Bet the IRS checks into that! I did get an online one emailed.

resp.text: Thank you for leaving us a review Ms. Mary!  We do apologize for the open window, as sometimes housekeeping does open them to air the room out before the next guest checks in.  We do have tub stoppers and rubber bathmats available at the front desk upon request for those that would like to take a hot bath.  Our 1 double bed rooms are listed online as a "small room" in the room description because they are a smaller room than the other room types we offer.  They are also the least expensive room type we offer for that very reason.  Our breakfast room is located down 1 flight of stairs, however, we do offer a full menu of our breakfast offerings for those that cannot make the stairs.  Our front desk can take the guest's order and deliver it right to the room.  Regarding the "no receipt at checkout", when guests book through a 3rd party booking site such as Expedia, Hotels.com, or Hotwire.com, those sites have you pay for the room at the time of booking it, so the actual hotel doesn't have a receipt to give you.  You would get your receipt from the website you booked the room through, as you had paid them not us.  Normally when booking through 3rd party websites, your confirmation of the reservation is your receipt.  That is why the clerk told you we couldn't give you a receipt, because you did not pay us directly for the room.  That goes for any hotel anywhere, just to clarify.  Thank you again for taking the time to leave us valuable feedback about your stay, and we hope you will come back to stay with us the next time you are in town.

resp.text: We really appreciate you giving us a review about your recent stay experience.  The type of room you had booked was a single room with 1 queen bed, which is listed online as a "small room", and is in fact a small room, but perfect for 1 person or a couple. name: G Aquino
text:
I'll give this hotel 3.5 stars. We chose it mainly for the price. Montpelier hotels are crazy expensive and this is one of the more reasonably priced ones and is close enough to the city. And I thought we got what we paid for.

Breakfast was filling but it's the same fare every single day. The room was comfortable and clean during check-in and had everything we needed (microwave oven, fridge, to name a few). The indoor pool with a hot tub was a nice bonus.

There were a few things that were not satisfactory. Some of the furnishings are falling apart and the water from the tap was murky brown one day. I would definitely advise against drinking from the tap. There aren't enough parking spots for all guests so if you arrive late, you'll end up at the overflow parking next to the hotel, which is not well-lit at night.

This type of thing bothers me so much because there's always one extra and it creates this awkward social situation at the table. Just give us 6 or 8.  Pizza was good, very traditional Italian inspired flavors and the dough was very good. Nothing to write home about but it was a good meal. It should be said that the atmosphere was awesome, really nice decor and the whole firehouse history is pretty cool.

text: Great food, terrible service. The restaurant has a nice, historic atmosphere and the food is very good. We had a party of five, everyone was happy with their meals. However, the service was horrendous. It was slow, inconsistent and simply poor. The waitress was reaching over people to serve dishes when their was no need as there was plenty of room to walk around to the next person. There were no "check ins" on our drinks or appetizers, drinks sat empty, plates not cleared. The kitchen was horrifically slow, what should have been an hour and fifteen minute meal turned into a 2 hour 45 minute ordeal. Service was simply poor. The waitress was very nice, apologizing for the waits, but it wasn't enough to overcome the bad service. I think the kitchen was terribly slow and the waitress was not properly trained.

My husband didn't like his burger (but LOVED the fries) and didn't make a big deal about it but Emily had wonderful customer service and took our dessert (an amazing maple apple crisp) off the bill without us even asking let alone thinking about it. It's hard to find such great service these days and so with these guys above and beyond what we were expecting of them was refreshing.  I definitely reccomend them to anyone who wants some awesome food,  chill atmosphere and friendly service.  Also, their bathrooms were immaculate. text:
An excellent Italian restaurant. The best in the area.
The staff is courteous and friendly, as well as helpful.
The menu has a wide variety of wonderful items.
Lunches or dinners, you'll find great food.
Expect a crowded restaurant because of the great food.
I haven't been to the restaurant this year, live out of state...staying home during these crazy times.
But, don't let that stop you from going to Sarducci's.

And don't forget, if you like this review please press the like button!

name: David Rapacz
text:
It’s an honest and deserved 3 1/2stars, but I can’t mark it that way...
Sat outside tonight by the river. They were following all guidelines and we were at least 9’ from the next table. Friend had Mussels that were excellent, and Seafood ravioli that he did not share “because it was that good”! The Mista Salad that came with my Chicken Park was really good; quite simple, but the greens were fresh, a couple olives and grape tomatoes, and there was a lot of Bluecheese which is A-OK with me! (I don’t know if that’s because I got BlueC dressing or if it’s on all of them.)
My Chicken Parm was not impressive, but ok. It was a little limp and there was nothing crispy at all. It taste OK, but definitely not note worthy. Can on Penne and sauce, also pretty just ok.
Cheesecake was Standard with frozen strawberries.
My Chianti was also not great, and filled with sediment...
I’ll be back. Not just because it’s kinda the only Italian around, but it was all-in-all good, it was a nice place to sit, and our waitress was great. Her name is Celeste. She’s new to VT; be nice! She was fast and professional, courteous and helpful, and absolutely adorable. I know that’s absolutely irrelevant and possibly inappropriate, but she was great and got The Ducc an extra, well earned, 1/2 a star. She really did make our meal a little nicer.
I say Give them a try.

name: Mary Czanysz
text: Sarducci's is a lively restaurant with a professional menu and staff. I do love the pizza, but that's not what draws me. It's the rest of the classics-plus menu. Get the risotto! I love the way they do the salmon in the light white win caper sauce, which is just so good.

name: Eric Rajendra
text:
Bustling place popular with locals as there aren’t too many nice dining options here in Montpelier.

Some good main dishes, some so-so...so I suggest you come 2-3 times and find what YOU like. The Salmon Cucina with capers and a great sauce was my favorite!!

Pizzas are generally great and crispy thin but if the cook of the day is fairly new it may come out burned a bit!!

Great drinks and wine (and desserts if you are into sugar highs!!).

Service is very prompt and generally not pushy to rotate your table!!

Try getting a table on the covered back balcony winter or summer with a great view of our Winooski River!!  Very busy at peak Vermont eating frenzy times (5 to 7 pm) so call to book a table so you get seated quickly!! After those times you can get a table easily!

Overall a great dining experience and for watching natives in their element!!

name: Sean Powell
text:
REALLY tasty Italian food.

You'll definitely want to reserve seating at least a few hours in advance, maybe even a day or two in advance if you plan on going on one of their busy weekend nights.

The food is outrageously tasty, and the pricing is honestly competitive for how great the food is.

One thing to also be aware of is that this place is VERY popular. Expect it to be packed, and not a quiet environment. It's a great place for food and drinks, but not if you aren't prepared for the noise/crowd.

name: christian mortuus est
text:
The Lanes
If you have been bowling anywhere else in the last 20-30 years you will realize this is an average establishment. The seating is uncomfortable and awkward for groups of people. The computerized scoring is outdated.
Have you ever bowled any place in the Midwest such as Detroit or Southern Ohio? They know how to keep up on maintenance, add modern conveniences without sacrificing nostalgic charm while providing a quality experience.

The Food
This is where the establishment exceeds expectations. Friendly service and decent prices. Thank you.

The Music
The seldom play music here which is odd. When they do it is pop music and usually not loud enough to actually hear anything. Bit of a wasted opportunity.

The Guns
The owner and/or manager has crated a gun-friendly environment. Less than a year ago some Neanderthal thought it wise to open-carry a pistol WHILE bowling. I understand the laws in VT around gun ownership and what is permissible...which is just about anything.
I approached the manager on what was a busy evening and ask if they could, for the benefit of everyone else there is a birthday party dozens children bowling, politely ask the patron to disarm - put the gun away. They said they could not legally do that.
Actually, you can if it is your establishment. You can ask a patron to not bowling while open-carry. You can ask any customer to remove themselves if they are perceived as a threat or liability. A civil conversation does not have to be adversarial but wise enough to know the difference between owner's rights, owner's responsibilities and everybody else in your establishments rights to enjoy an afternoon of gun-free fun.

Closing...
I bowl here frequently. Not many other options living in Central Vermont. Other than the gun related issues at this local, it is a great space. Two star because guns ruin even the best of times.

Bowl on!
Keep your guns at home.

text: We arrived ordered our food and realized we had been waiting for half hour for food so I finally went to ask what was going on and they lost our order. The food was amazing I suggest trying the pulled pork. We also went to get ice cream after we ate our food and she didn't charge us for that either. Great customer service at this place like some of the best I have seen around this area. They let us finish without disturbing us even after they had locked there doors for the night. name: F. Grymes
text:
Do you enjoy grocery shopping? Well of course you do!! And I mean, WHO doesn't?? Well for all you grocery shopping lovers out there, and even for all you haters out there, this Hannafords is where you want to be!! The store is well organized, good vegi selection, decent deli wait lines (doncha love waiting in line for sandwich fixings), good seafood and meat variety, relatively clean and super friendly staff!! Great local beer selection, and local vegetables are an added bonus.
So take a trip to Hannafords and smile, even with a mask on, they will know. Tell them you appreciate the hard work they put in, risking their lives, to provide the public with essentials.
THANK YOU Hannaford staff

text:
I was so happy to walk in here the day after visiting the world's saddest Price Chopper in nearby Colchester.  This grocer is conveniently located amongst other shopping and also a liquor store.

This Hannaford is pretty decent and should fulfill most of your grocery shopping needs.  I like that the store is somewhat renovated and kept up too, it's not all that different than the one in my hometown in the suburbs of Albany, NY.

The produce section was very nice and they even have multiple Kombuchas on tap.

I'd describe the bakery section as average, but it's handy if you are in a pinch.  The breads for sale looked nice.

We spotted sushi, hot food bar and an olive bar.  This is Vermont, so they had a nice selection of maple syrups.

Our visit was quick since we only needed a couple of things, but this was a well stocked grocery spot.

text:
I visit this grocery store several times a week. It's a nice, clean store that carries a variety of groceries. I wish that they would do a better job at keeping certain products stocked. Often times I go in to find two or three items on my list unavailable until their next delivery.
For the most part the employees are friendly and very helpful. I've had a couple of unpleasant interactions at this store, but typically any problems that arise are resolved quickly and efficiently.
I love the store policies! If something is wrong with one of their Hannaford brand products or even if you just don't like the taste of a Hannaford item you bought, they will not only refund your money but give you DOUBLE the cash back. I buy a lot of Hannaford brand Items now, knowing that if I don't care for it I can simply do a return or exchange.

She also allows the customer at the quick checkout to attempt to run the same food stamp card 5 times even though it has CLEARLY said 5x that there is not enough funds! She allows the customer at the only other register to slowly go back through her CART FULL of grocery bags one bag at a time and allows this customer to just stand there debating each individual item in her cart! This is a common theme in the Burlington area, where management knows absolutely nothing about TRUE CUSTOMER SERVICE!! Hannaford needs to be much more selective of the employees they hire as they are the faces of their company! Im pretty sure Hannaford lost at least 20 customers last night due to the serious, complete lack of customer service, ESPECIALLY  coming from a "manager"!!

text:
I have YET to stop to this McDonalds and NOT have an issue of varying severity after examining my usually simple orders. Forgotten French fries, forgotten condiments, forgotten burgers, forgotten modifications to a sandwhich...  I mean this is literally EVERYTIME . So, if it's happening to me all the time,  it's happening to a lot of people.
I used to manage restaurants for a living. From the ages of 22 until 37. Obviously there is an issue with this place, but come on. I cant sit here knowing how a restaurant is ran, and be upset with the young adults who are working and most likely the ones who mistakenly mis-handle or mis-pack the to go bag. I do however, blame management for not being more aware of the problem, and not addressing the issue.
I hope this McDonalds improved, as it's the only one within 35 miles. But, I think I'm going to be hitting up the Burger King across the street instead from now on.

text: One of our favorite places to shop. We have a pastry chef in the house so this is a must stop and shop place. I get him a gift card here or 3 or 400 dollars every year. If you were any kind of a baker this is the place to go if you can't make it here you can certainly shop online but it's always fun to come here they do have a nice cafe as well. Of course through the covid it's kind of you know pretty limited right now. text: King Arthur Flour is a great place to buy baking supplies. If you go for lunch on a busy day, you can wait a long time for it.  If you get there at a good time, lunch will come pretty quickly.  I just had a "Special" lunch that completely missed the mark - the Sweet Potato Cakes on a bed of lemony slaw were completely dried up discs (slightly bigger than a quarter -3 of them) on a plate of shredded red cabbage and kale - barely drizzled with tatziki.  If you go for a meal, you might be best off with their tried and true regular menu items.

name: Stephanie Pineiro
text: Great place to grab coffee, dessert, or lunch! Fantastic pastries and coffee. The bakery has a lot of seating and the staff are so friendly.

name: Carol DelGaudio
text: Excellent quality baking supplies. Friendly, knowledgeable staff

name: Craig Woody
text: Great food and service

name: Jonathan Forrest
text: I love the great and me unique selection of baking tools and ingredients. The restaurant and bakery is fantastic. But, I was a little disappointed that I couldn't have my BLT on sourdough bread though they had fresh sourdough loaves for sell.

name: Raz
text: Great place to get a bite, a cup of coffee or tea and a pastry to go. If you are planning to do some work that requires you have high-speed WiFi, then it is NOT the place to be.

name: Roger Simmons
text: Today was a visit for a baking class. KAF does a "Family Dinner Night" most Fridays where a family (or group of 4) comes in and does a 2.5 hour baking centric cooking class. Tonight we did fresh pasta and a "sauce" along with cookies (they also provide a salad) which you then take home. The class is well done if fast paced and of course you go home with food, an education and afun experience. 5 STARS!

name: Kim Murphy
text: Great experience and a fun afternoon.  Loved learning a new skill and tasting or creations.

name: Cameron Dale MacQuarrie
text: great food. great coffee. great shop. great people

name: Rohit Shah
text: An amazing experience visiting the factory. Cafe  offers some great sandwich, brakefast and baked goods. Gift shop is outstanding. Every imaginable baking item was available for the purchase. Some great baking cook books selection in the store. Lot of classes to learn baking skills. Staff is friendly and knowledgeable. Highly recommend place to visit.

name: Ian Hefele
text: Finally made it here but felt like Ben and Jerry's for Flour

name: jesse shaw
text: Came across this place by chance when on vacation.  Just thought we were going to grab coffee, breakfast sandwich, and a treat.  4 hours later.  The food was great, we tried many things because we weren't going to be back for a while, and everything was better than the last.  There is an outdoor area to allow kids to burn off their sugar intake. The marketplace was fun to explore and the kids could watch the bakers bake for hours. Only complaint was the coffee was mediocre.

name: John Holzinger
text: Not as many goodies as before

name: Julie's bites
text: We bought some great tasting bread and pastries.  A large variety of breads and pastries are sold here. Several pleasant area to sit down and have a snack, both inside and outside.  The store has a large variety of baking tools, mixes, spices and jams.  There is also a very nice bathroom.

name: Alexander J
text: Great concept, good food but terribly designed layout of the cafe that leads to very long wait times. 15 minute minimum for coffee, not a joke.

name: truetexas
text: Nice little cafe, gift shop and baking school.

name: Jennifer Schelly
text:
Awesome place! Love the cafe, love the classes, love the store. -1 star for the huge (and slow moving) lines at the cafe.

Parents: Step stools and stairs for the kids to see into the bakery windows. Kids table and chairs in the cafe.

EV drivers: Charging station not in the main parking lot. Follow the service and deliveries sign to the further south entrance from the main road. Chargers are next to the solar array.

Hikers/walkers: Little trail from the main parking lot.

name: Tara Lulla
text: Great selection of products

name: Luna Dunbar
text: The markup on kitchen gadgets and tools is fairly high, but its a good place to get some of their harder to find flours.  Lots of gluten free flours and box mixes.

name: Davide Buck
text: Very expensive, pizza is not good! Coffee is bad,water taste strange,Pastry is good, the bread quality is getting worst, and they treat the kitchen workers very bad!!! Just like a corporation would, for an employee owned company they make the workers feel like they don’t even own themselves! Rude people. I hope in the future they can find their humanity again because they where a good business in the past.

name: Michelle Gianakos
text: This place is a baker's dream come true!

name: Katherine Mayerovitch
text: I'm pretty sure this is what heaven smells like. As soon as you walk in the door, it hits you: the scent of fresh baked bread. The environment is rustic, but the building is modern on the sly. There are always families with kids here, students and professionals working on their laptops (WiFi is free and pretty reliable, if a bit on the slow side) and people meeting up for business or pleasure. There are cold sandwiches or tubs of soup if you'd like to grab and go, or get something made for a snack or a meal and enjoy the space. Honestly, you need to get the bread and jam for breakfast sometime. There's nothing more beautifully local in every way.

name: Bev Owen
text: King Arthur Flour is an excellent place to grab a coffee, lunch or dessert or all of them!  The prices are reasonable. Get it to go or dine in and use the free reliable WiFi. The staff is wonderful.  They know just how I like my mocha latte and they never question my oddities. They always have a smile on their faces and it's really great that they take the time to remember a name.  Great atmosphere and they even have a shop in the same building as the bakery. Ample parking. Outside dining.  Highly recommend KAF. Enjoy!

name: Richard Horning
text: Doing it right 👍

name: Stephen Schad
text: Love the bakery and the store.  Great sandwiches, pizza and baked goods.  Love the almond cloud cookies and the whoopie pies.  The store has a lot of good baking supplies and a lot of mixes.  Be prepared to spend a lot of money.

name: Mark Stacy
text: This place is a foodie icon! Great food in the Cafe, very pleasant enviroment. A great group of some of the finest bakers on the east coast. The store is amazing and carries fine baking implements and supplies. When you're in the area, you must visit!

name: Emily Pogozelski
text:
I've been coming to the Cafe since they opened, and was a fan of the store even back when it was in a tiny building before this beautiful new complex was built. This is a MUST VISIT for any baker, and the Cafe has more than enough to satisfy anyone. A few favorites: 5 Seed Sourdough is SPECTACULAR, the jalapeño cheddar spread (in the refrigerator case) makes for the best sandwiches, the egg sandwiches are hearty and filling (only til 11am! Get there early!) and the Cinnamon Rolls are TO.DIE.FOR. Those sell out by mid-morning many days, so be sure to get there early if you're really craving one.

Friendly and efficient service, plus the company is employee owned, so you know they really care. Love this place! Check it out!

name: Jake
text: Great food and cool gift shop. Wish there was a wider selection of sandwiches though. We hope to come back for a class someday. Also got a chance to charge my car!

name: Joshua Moore
text: We love this place!

name: David Bridges
text: Great lunch. Great baking shop. They definitely need more lunch seating.

name: Steve Lipofsky
text:
Just a bakery Wonderland.

Just took a pizza making course there and it exceeded all my expectations.

A delightful experience. I learned a lot!

name: Diane Lagarto
text: Not only Great bread with opportunities to see it being made but a place to get healthy fresh home cooked food and the store...has everything you could want, even if you want gluten free! Stop in for soup, sandwich, shopping. You'll be glad you did!

name: Joseph Shaw
text: Not fully open

name: Ivan Zajicek
text: Amazing breakfast and lunch options with very friendly and patient staff!

name: David Donegan
text: Holiday Chocolate Almond Tree Cakes, need I say more?

name: Robert Allaway
text: Great spot. Wish the breakfast sandwiches were on portugese muffins and not brioche rolls!

name: Colleen Newton Pause
text: If you like to bake, you will LOVE KAF Store; if you like to eat, you will LOVE the Cafe.

name: JJ Harrison
text: Great breads and baking products

name: Norman Rohr
text: You gotta love them.

name: John Horrocks
text: Always good food. Always a pleasure to see Laura. Staff great good drinks n Covid safe protocol. Look forward to next time.

name: Sal
text:
We arrived at noon, a crowd quickly was forming. The couple in front of us was asked, do you have reservation? They didn't, she took them to their table. We are asked same question, No, I tried to call. She scoffed and sat the 6 of us. Place is filling up, we spend 20 min reviewing menu before asked for our order or drinks. Others are already eating and drinking. Place our order, another 25 min and food arrives.
Fish and Chip, special, wasn't cooked completely. The 3 stone filet mignon, hot sizzling stones. The seas scallops stone, barely sizzles when scallop placed. Seemed to cool pretty quick, she offered me another stone, I asked for it to be seared in the kitchen, it was back in 2 minutes. The slaw was sour and brown, the asparagus was cold and the fries slightly warm.
The place is now full, I hear our server apologizing to others, sorry I forgot your iced tea, sorry I forgot you were there. We won't be back. Stick to the steak in a steak house is our rule of thumb, and I won't forget that at another steakhouse though. Had a lot of people tell us to go here, it wasn't the same experience they obviously enjoyed to recommend.
My daughter said a little flavor on the steak would have been better,  but at least her stone sizzled and the meat was soft. We didn't feel welcomed or that our server was friendly.

name: Dave's Adventures
text: I had forgotten that reservations were necessary, but the staff found us a table anyway. The server was super friendly and attentive. The food was well prepared, hot, and tasty. The popovers were excellent with the accompanying honey butter. This was an excellent visit.

name: Todd Jackson
text: Service is a bit slow 🐌 but the food is excellent at a very affordable price!

name: Dave Churchill
text: Family run place with great food--always something you don't normally see at other places on the menu.  Good prices and great beer and cocktails--say Hi to Shannon and you better say hi to Nana if she's there too!  :)

name: C.T. Black
text:
$$$. Very pricey so be ready, but an experience worth paying for. Never seen a black lava rock you cook your own dinner (meat) on. It was a great meal. The ribeye took a little too long to cook where it was the so thick. Filet and Ny strip did better.

Drinks were good. Very small town sitting and nicely decorated restaurant. Staff was friendly and quick.

Salad bar is great as well. Lots of options. We all skipped apps since they had a salad bar.

name: Lynx Brammer
text: This place may be expensive, but it's worth every penny. We went on Sunday and had a "special" of prime rib.  About 10oz, they said. What I got can be seen below in the photo and that was taken after 3 or 4 bites. And don't balk at the upcharge for adding a salad bar. It is a meal in itself with soup, traditional salad, potato, chicken, and pasta salad, plenty of fixings, breads and cheese.

name: Steven Gerow
text: Very good meal all around from salad bar to baked potato. Friendly service. Good cuts of meat. Very busy but don't take reservations.

name: Cory Curtis
text: Burger was literally burnt! I asked for well done not a hockey puck! Also very pricey.

name: Tammie Morrison
text: Food was delicious! Service was stellar! Prices reflected the quality of the food.

name: Andrew Obierek

name: Daniel Zee

name: Carol Flint

text: Delicious. Wonderful presentation! Good selection.  Might have gotten a 5☆ if waitress had set table and checked in on us . Didn't even  offer  desert menu  and I ♡deserts!

name: Patricia Clark

name: J. Smith
text:
We drove from RANDOLPH twice to eat here.
First time I had halibut & it was supposed to be cooked with spicy seasoning.   I requested the cook leave that off & he/she did.  Cooked perfectly with salt, pepper & something green.

Husband got the Prime rib, again, cooked to perfection.   Both of us had the rice pilaf & it was flavorful & we each got another vegetable that also was VERY good.

Nice was friendly & took good care of us.  The BEST place we ate at in Vermont!  HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

name: Roy Duclos
text: Best steak I've ever eaten. If you like your steak more than medium rare have them cook it for you. I like mine a little more than rare and they put it on a 500 degree Black Rock and it Cooks in front of you. Great staff and attractive setting. They have seafood as well. Will be trying the lobster on my next trip. A bit pricy but worth every penny.

name: sawta none
text:
It was a really great place. The staff was pleasant, the atmosphere was great, the prices were good and the food was very nice. Heck, even the seats for the booths were comfy!

You're missing out if you don't give this place a try.

name: Bruce Cheeney
text: Went again to black rock it was very good. Good price good food. Great server. Going to try again soon.

name: Paige Gale
text: First time here. AMAZING food and outstanding service. Great  atmosphere. Very clean. Great drinks. My boyfriend who’s never had a margarita seemed addicted to them. Everything was spectacular, right down to the lightening and music. The bar was great and the overall experience was definitely deserving of 5 stars ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️

name: Tina Smrkovski
text: Steaks, King Crab, and Salad Bar. Add in a drink for a great meal. Recommend coming early or plan for a bit if a wait. They are usually busy!

name: Roberto Diaz
text: Very good

name: Danielle Hammond
text: We had went in hoping to get nachos and some pub food. What we had was great but it cost 3 times what we planned on spending. Didn't find out the other menu still existed until after the meal. And you have to specifically ask for it. Service was great and everything, I just feel like that's a bit shady. The waitress was great but are you trying to make a ton of extra money from tips off people by avoiding handing the pub menu out?? She did the same thing she'd have done it we had ordered off the other menu, less actually, because we'd have got an appetizer too, plus drinks, and she'd have brought that out. Instead we ordered only entrees. And she had to only carry out that. So she made more money for less work... Good food, and we may go back, but we both felt a little put off by that... :/ maybe just tuck the pub menus in the regular ones so people don't feel like you're pulling a fast one?

name: Charles Kramp
text:
Great taste and fun at the same time.
Love the Argentinian on the rock with Rosemary and sea salt.  Each piece cooked to  your exact preference as you do it yourself.  Consistently great.

name: Vt-Hobo
text: Very good seafood,  nice wait staff, and pleasant atmosphere. Definitely worth the trip

name: Brandie Slicer
text: Nice salad bar. They have actual black rocks you can cook your steaks/ Ahi-Tuna on. It's pretty fun! Be sure to read the directions in the menu, or ask for advice- the rocks are 750F  Temp! The seafood was fresh and delicious, service was great!

name: Nia Shadowstalker
text: Lovely service and excellent food. We had the seafood bake for my birthday and it was dreamy. The swordfish was melt in your mouth buttery good.

name: Melissa Olund
text: Outstanding!

name: Henry Guiles
text: In my opinion this is the best steakhouse in the state of Vermont.  Steak served on a hot lava rock with unlimited salad bar and soup for $25. It's a bit noisy and hard to get a table sometimes, but it's worth the wait. I highly recommend this place. The waitstaff is attentive and friendly and the decor is tasteful. Nothing bad to say, really.

name: Martha Dole-Rietta
text: This is my second review. The first was 4 stars. Lunch was very disappointing. First i have to say, our waitress was outstanding...but then on to lunch...Soggy veggies and overcooked salmon (very dry and burnt on the bottom) i tried the creme brulee hoping it wouldnt be burnt this time but once again, i was disappointed

text: This is my favorite steakhouse in Vermont. Having your steak cooked on the rock is amazing. You have to try it!

name: Realistic Reality
text: Great seafood, this from someone who's  not from landlocked state. One of the few places I'll order it from & I am not just speaking of fish & chips.

name: Mason Kaehler
text: Amazing food and service. Wonderful steak :)

name: Raymond Makul
text:
I have lunch here about once a week.  There's a regular printed menu, and blackboard specials.  I usually have something in the seafood group.  The food is good and plentiful.   The waitresses know me on sight, and have my usual drink waiting for me.

Prices for a blackboard special lunch is not much more than at the fast food place down the street, but the food is ten times better.  Great food and great staff.

name: Delightfully Me
text: Filet mignon served right!! Great salad bar. The crispest onion rings, delicious!

name: George blood
text: One of my favorite local places to go,,for the Vets out there before you walk in front door look across the street..flag do display of all the branches of the armed Forces with the beautiful Vermont background.

name: Laurie Skinner
text: Huge variety of salad bar, good value

name: Zachary Welch
text: Why pay $30.00 for a steak when YOU have to cook it. It says that there steaks weigh a certin amount but....  Minus the bone it weighs under a pound. Burgers are dry as the Gobby  Desert.  Grill needs to be clean and wait staff could be a little keen of being hostest . They charge an arm and leg for everything. The salad bar was good . A very tight small place good luck getting a seat if you dare to go

name: Courtney Griffin
text: Good variety of food and well cooked

name: Sonja Stefan
text: Terrific service, salad bar was DIVINE and the clam chowder was definitely their own...best I've tasted with a little"kick"! My husband had strip steak and I had filet mignon and both were EXCELLENT.

name: Hans Hammarquist
text: I can't really give an honest review as I went there, invited to a Thanksgiving dinner. The dinner was very good. Most of the time I dredge these dinners as the turkey usually is tasteless and dry. Here I got served a delicious turkey, very tasty, very tender and not that "woodfiber" like meat you frequently experience. I really liked it and enjoyed it. If this is the way the kitchen always prepare their food I can highly recommend this place. The restaurant stile is rustic, a place you can show up at in T-shirt and dungarees.

name: Tom Whalen
text: Great selection of food at reasonable prices with satisfying portions. Having your steak cooked on a black rock at your table is really neat!

name: Steph Fowler

name: Bruce Monroe

text: Cooking your own filet on a hot rock has to be one of the best ways to guarantee satisfaction. The taste and overall experience is awesome. The salad bar is well worth the extra $4 and includes soup, breads, cheese wheel and many items not found on many salad bars. The chocolate fondue is the ultimate end to such a good meal.

During one visit we had the pleasure of listening to the manager verbally assault one of the wait-staff for some trivial reason. I think they keep management out back now which makes for a better dining experience for everyone else. The salad bar is decent. Stay away from anything fried, their batter is horrible - it is dense like tempura and is dripping with grease that is sure to upset your stomach... But like I said, the black rock steak is fantastic!

name: Sarah Gagliardi

name: Tom Behan
text:
Very good place to eat
Last night I had a 23oz Porter house with pelof. It comes with a salad bar. The salad bar is to die for.  My wife has some type of chi Ken with a mushroom artichoke sauce on it.  She chose a baked potato and sour cream.  She also has a Cesar salad.  We were too stuffed for desert.  Portions are perfect size.  The place is all about beef.  So if you beef, you will love this place.  Expect to wait around 30 to 40 minutes.  Call ahead before you go to see how long the wait is.  They only take reservations for groups of 6 or more.  You will not be disappointed.  This is the second time I have been there.  They also serve tons of fresh seafood as well.  King grab legs, lobsters, king kreo crab legs, claims bakes, broied, breaded,steamed.  You name it they do it. They also have oysters raw of cooked.  The have escargot as well.  It's an around the town steak house but has fancy pieces here and there.  It is the only one in the area.  Try it you will love it.

text: It's a good place to get a cheap dinner out (comparatively to going to a "nice" place in the area), but expect low quality standards. I've found long blonde hairs in the salad bar's bread loaves more than once. Their kitchen staff clearly do not use hairnets and it's a continual issue, which is deeply disgusting, BUT, the food is quite good, so long as you get lucky and don't get someone's hair in your mouth. If they just had higher standards for staff, requiring hairnets in the kitchen, I'd give it a higher rating, but the hair in the food is really gross. The food is good enough, the appetizers are excellent (especially the stuffed mushrooms), the seafood is cooked correctly, the entrees are usually decent but beef and chicken can come out improperly cooked (usually overcooked). Their Cesar salad is fantastic, their dressing is second to none. Pity about the lacking kitchen standards. We still eat there, but I now tend to avoid the bread. Is isn't very good bread anyway, so no great loss. They should just buy it pre-made elsewhere since they can't make it without getting hair in it and it's not even very good. The desserts are TERRIBLE, don't bother ordering any of them, they are flat out awful. You're better off buying a box of Little Debbies at the grocery afterwards.

And if you want novelty, order your entree "on the rock". We watched our friend cook his own Ahi tuna steak, slice by slice, on a flat black rock, right at the table.
All this fun and yumminess at surprisingly low prices! We'll definitely go back any time we're in the area.

At this time the ceaser salad came out which was 20% peppercorns. Almost 20 minutes after that I got my n.y. strip steak, and my girlfriend got her chicken cordon bleu. For the first time since I can remember I actually had to ask for steak sauce to go with it. My "medium" steak was still bloody in the middle. My side of broccoli in cheese sauce was 4 pieces of broccoli in what seemed like melted Velveeta. To top all of this off the waitress barely apologized in passing for any of this, and we did not see a manager. They also pay $5.79 per bottle of A1 steak sauce. name: Rick Boyle
text: Very nice location and the rooms are very nice as well. Unfortunately, due to the covid reactions, a lot of the amenities are closed. But still a pleasant stay.

name: Michael Reynolds
text: Great accommodations on the best ski resort.

text: I attended a conference there and it was great. I really enjoyed the whole environment.

name: Shawn Anderson
text: Beautiful place.  We had a great time at the wedding he Wine and Fall Festival

name: Russ Perna
text: The rooms were spacious and we'll maintained. The hotel spa, pool, and other amenenities we're all top notch. The staff went above and beyond at every step. Definitely highly recommend this hotel.

name: Wylie Carlisle
text: Beautiful spot. The road crew is great. No trouble driving or parking. Let was clear and easy to drive in. Very well maintained with salt and sand.

name: Anthony LoFrisco Jr
text: A nice, newer hotel that is right off the mountain, on the other side of the tubing hill. Nice lobby and restaurant with good food. It's expensive, especially during busy season. The hotel staff is friendly, engaging and helpful. My only major beef is there is no bar. Really?? A ski lodge with no bar is dumbfounding and a huge miss on their part. Good thing there are plenty of places with good food and drink very close by.

name: Adam Corrigan
text: Overall this place is my favorite place to stay while visiting the mountain. Great amenities including, valet parking, ski check, outdoor pool and hot tubs, spa, and gym. It feels a little old overall and is due for a renovation but unfortunately that will probably mean the prices will go up. Right now it is a pretty good value. The restaurant downstairs, Harriman's is pretty good but overpriced. Unfortunately this is your only option for dinner at the hotel.

name: Chris Larsen
text: Mount Snow is a great family mountain.  The skiing is as good as you're gonna get in the area - great snow making and good work grooming (and not grooming when they can!).  The owners continue to put more money into the resort every year.  Get another high speed chair in Sunbrook and the North Face!  Trails for all levels; good clinics for kids and adults.  Good beers on tap.  Not sure there's much else you need.

name: Brandon Dorman
text: Very nice hotel and great staff. Loved being there

name: Regina Perrotto
text: Nice place. The womens locker room could be cleaner in summer.

name: Liana M
text: Grand Country Deli at the Grand Summit Hotel makes MEAN sandwiches!! Addicted!

name: Jeff Bassett
text: Great mountain!! Love the terrain and the vibe. Always feels like I'm home when I'm there.

name: Princess K

text: Was here for the Wine Fest. $20 For a glass and 3 tickets was a little steep. 1 ticket got you a tasting at a single vendor and there were way more vendors than tickets. Also as expected there was also a good amount of entertainment.

text: Lacks charm.  My expectations of a VT 'resort' are so much higher than the physical facility can deliver.  The people are great; the building/architecture/design not so much.

text: This is a great local deli with plenty of fresh options. They are a bit pricey and they throw a lot of bread at you, so if you're on a diet it's not really a great place to go. However if you do like bread this bread is by far the best and freshest in the area. They have a nice outdoor sitting area and the seating inside is comfortable and cozy. The food is very good overall and the service is friendly.

name: B.J. Loveislove
text: Just love this deli. Have returned many times. Delicious sandwiches made to order on fresh homemade bread, some desserts/cookies available, salads in self help case available, great people. Clean bathroom.

text: Our stay at the Equinox is better than expected.  The room we had at the 1811 House was charming, yet they upgraded where it counts like the bathroom. The staff was so helpful and kind. I recommend staying here, especially like us, we are Vermonters and wanted to have a two day away from home and work, but stay Covid Safe. Now just need to start a fire in our room.

resp.text:
Hello Fellow Vermonter,
Thank you for your kind review. I am so happy you are enjoying your stay and will pass along this wonderful feedback to the rest of our team.  Our goal is to create an incredible and safe experience for all of our guests. On behalf of all the staff at the Equinox Resort, please reach out if we can further assist you during your stay,

name: Amelia G
text: Lovely place. To use the pool, during covid-19, you must reserve a spot, but you can usually get a reservation for every day you're at the hotel. Meals at breakfast and lunch aren't as good as dinner. Everyone on staff is helpful, and I know as they had to fix my room key more than once. The rooms are luxurious, and the resort has some very interesting amenities like the pool and spa. There is also lots of property to explore, plus an adorable park for the little ones.

resp.text: Hi Amelia, I am thrilled you enjoyed your stay. Thank you for your kind review, we hope to welcome you back again soon.

name: Robert Rapatski
text: Beautiful place! Old hotel that sits at the base of the mountain. Great place to stay and host a wedding. The service was excellent and I enjoyed DJing here.

name: C.M. Jones
text: we would have liked to have stayed last week but they were pretty much booked solid that the fact that it was like about $600 a night kind of made me say no. I do have a bonavoy credit card which allows you a free night but in a hotel that expensive it doesn't pay for the whole thing I still would have had to cough up about $350.I have stayed there several times in the past when prices were a little more reasonable which they are different times of the year.of course with the covered now if you want to use the pool you have to sign up for it have to wait to do it can only go in for a 45 minute increment. Kind of takes a lot of the fun out of the whole thing.

text: Wonderful location, beautifully updated decor, incredible service and delicious, memory-making food. Will definitely stop by for dinner again if given the chance. The experience has also made me think about staying at the Equinox as a guest in the future.

text:
Wonderful resort property with excellent spa and service. We vacationed there with family of four and dog. There were many dogs there which was great for a family vacation.

Can be drafty in the cold weather as its a historic old property. But rooms are nicely renovated and nice fire in lounge and deck.

text: Great bar.  Great historic destination hotel.  Very pricey.  Classic.

name: Ron Mosocco
text: We visited here last September and found it to be magnificent! It is privately owned, purchase your ticket at the gift shop and make sure your brakes are working! The day we visited the view was spectacular, simply gorgeous as you can see from the photos I uploaded here. Such a beautiful early fall day! I highly recommend you plan your visit around good weather. I don't advise you spending your money, time and hazard on foggy or rainy days.  Quiet and serene to ponder Mother Nature's beauty. As the Who sang, I can see for miles and miles and miles!  Enjoy and drive slowly on the way back down! You will find this place has a religious connection and overtones.

name: Amelia G
text: The drive was beautiful, and the downhill felt fast, even though we went  less than 20 mph. Nice rest stops to get out and take pictures. Make sure to come on a cloudless day, so you can see everything. It's really fun, and some people actually hike up the mountain, which seems kind of crazy, but is very healthy, I'm sure. It is a must see when nearby.

text: The views are worth it though the entry fee is steep.  After driving to the top of Mt. Equinox you encounter a modern building where you can take in the sights from or you can roam around the property outside.  There is a trail or two at the top which offer the same beauty and less people.  Beware of the black flies that swarm you, our family had a few bites and they are not fun.

name: Josef & Cindy Martin
text: Incredible views...watch your brakes!

name: Michael Hayes Jr.
text: The views are beautiful especially during the fall.  The monastery is hard to see from the market but if you go farther up the mountain you can see it better.

name: Roy Nunn
text: This is a nice 5 mile drive up Equinox Mountain to the St. Bruno Scenic Viewing Center.  Pull into the parking lot at the entrance to pay and get some info about the road and Viewing Center at the top.  It is an easy ride with plenty of turn outs to stop, take in the view, and let the car cool down a little.  We went up in early October, the views were great up to about half way, then the clouds obstructed all views, but it was still worth the drive.  (The people in the Toll House did warn us that we would see anything as we got closer to the top, but we wanted to go up anyway.)

name: Rohit Shah
text: Beautiful views of mountains of Vermont. A must drive to the top. The road going to the top is twisty and has some sharp turns. But drive is worth. You pay at the entrance to enter the drive going up to the mountain. Parking at the ticket office seem cramped but may be due to holiday season. Too of the mountain parking is decent. 3 storied building to enjoy non obstructed views. Must visit place in Green mountains.

name: Tanim Imani
text: The highest mountain in southern Vermont with a gorgeous views.

name: Adirondack Eddie
text: 20 bucks to drive to summit but very nice

name: Edward Simpson
text: Mount Equinox is a nice hike with excellent views at the summit.   The hike to the summit is moderate but tge views are amazing.  I suggest you take a short walk to tge gravestone of Mr. Darbo b ear the scenic overlook. Google Darbo's owner, he had quite the life story.

name: Charles Beauchain

name: Lynn Cherry

name: Don Hoyt

name: Lis Oliveira

name: Amelia G
text: This was delicious. We were staying nearby, and came twice. I wish this were in my area! They were super flexible with taking different base parts out of the order. I got a taco with chicken, mushrooms and some other additions. It was all really delicious. Everyone in my group loved it so much and can't wait to be back!

name: Jo Morgan
text: Absolutely thrilled to have come across Cilantro! The taco’s are exceptional. Today I had the “Street Taco’s” meal deal. I went with chorizo and the jalapeño garlic chicken (special of the day). Both were aromatic and delicious. Everything is fresh and locally sourced. I’d highly recommend Cilantro if you want to grab a quick meal in Manchester.

name: Kelley Gardner
text: This used to be a hidden gem, but lately the lines have been long so you need to plan on 20 minutes or so to get your order.  Worth the wait if you have the time.

name: Christa Jan Ryan
text: Excellent Spanish food at reasonable prices!

name: Bob Jones
text: Hate to say it but it just isn’t as good as it used to be

name: Trevor Shatney
text: Arguably the best Mexican food available in Vermont, my wife and I regularly find ourselves craving their burritos, although their generous serving sides may be too much for the average human being. Fortunately, they come in mini sizes as well. Follow it up with some of the great chips they serve.

name: Dot Link
text: The street tacos are one of the tastiest, least expensive lunches in town. Salad with their house dressing is outstanding. Try the limeade too. So refreshing and almost buttery tasting. Environmentally conscious establishment. I love this place.

name: jesse shaw
text: Food was above average and very tasty.  Though it was a tad expensive and greasy. The employees were grumpy which had us worry about the food quality, but was very enjoyable.  The chips and salsa were also very good.

name: Pete K
text: Enjoyed tacos and burritos, filled with freshly prepared ingredients.  The burritos are large, with plenty of meat--enough to feed two people.  The tacos are soft, also generously filled, and served with beans and rice.  Canned craft beers are also available.

name: Rocio L. Baker
text: We love the food and how efficient the staff is. We love Cilantro!!!

name: Aaa Aaa
text: Usually a weekly go to for dinner.  All the food is fresh and made in front of you.  Highly recommend this one!

name: Angi Scudder
text: Great food!  Fun rustic decor and a great place for a really good taco

name: Jennifer Lee Donaker
text: Local restaurant with local ingredients. Laid back with some nice home made salsas. Funny name though given that I don't Think I saw any cilantro in my food (not complaining just pointing out, particularly if you don't like cilantro). I wish they had guacamole though! They only have sliced avocado. Great for a quick bite.

name: Nancy Black
text: Excellent service with tasty FRESH food.  Vegan AND gluten free options available too.....word up!! I came here 2x in the same wknd!

name: Kathleen Potts

name: Dave Rossman

name: Lyn Rinaldi

Cilantro touts a strong local/community-based focus locally sourcing ingredients whenever possible and in support of local charities. Menu offers build-your-own tacos and burritos with assorted meats, sauces, and toppings. My favorite, 1 Street Taco and 1 Americano Taco.

name: Caitlyn Arellano
text: Great food. Great service. Just wish there was more in the way of Vegetarian options

name: Will Goodwin

Awesome service! Fabulous good!
It wasn't too busy, came in for a Sunday afternoon noon brunch in September. Reception, hostess, bartender, server, and manager were all really friendly. The hotel is beautiful and decor created a great warm feeling.

Food was delicious - we started with the crispy chicken wings, dry rub. I wasn't sure if I would like them but wow. Super yum.

The Grouse Breakfast Sandwich was full of savory flavor, though I could see it being to heavy for some. The side salad lightly dressed helped cut through some of the heaviness. My husband got the Pastrami Smoked Salmon which he thought was good. We're from NYC so the bagel wasn't our favorite but good enough. Served with capers so that's a good touch. Father had the Copper Grouse burger, definitely great though the bun was a bit soft to hold all the beefy juicy goodness of the burger. Didn't stop him from finishing every last bite.

name: Rich Jurewicz
text:
Had an outstanding meal at the Reluctant Panther last night.  My entree of Switchback ale braised short ribs was tender and flavorful.  It came with smoked cheddar mashed potatoes, a shallot bacon marmalade and crispy brussel sprouts, all cooked to perfection.

My wife had the seared lamb loin. It was a generous portion, allowing her to bring some home for the next day to continue to enjoy its excellent flavors.

My fellow diners split a lobster and brie fondue appetizer, and all found it to be rich with tender pieces of lobster. It was enjoyed by each of them.

The flourless chocolate cake I had was a great way to end the meal.  Throw in what I thought was a generous pour of my malbec, it was an outstanding meal from start to finish. I highly recommend the Reluctant Panther and the innovative meal preparation of Chef Sigal Rocklin, a worthy recipient of Vermont's Chef of the Year award in 2018.

This was a brand new F airfield Inn.  I'm not sure when it was built, but everything was brand new.
The rooms were large, clean and comfortable and got the job done.  The kids enjoyed the pool and hot tub.  The morning breakfast was very good.
The staff was fantastic!  The woman at the front desk (I want to say Melanie, but I'm not sure...) happened to be working most of the shifts were there for 2 nights/3 days, and she was very helpful.  She helped us buy Stowe ski tickets on line (they are $20 cheaper) navigating the horrible Stowe web site and answered all our questions.  She recommended the Prohibition Pig for dinner and it was a big hit.
My son left his math book in the room once we left and when he called in a panic they told him they found it and were shipping it to our home address.
Highly recommend staying if you need a place in the area.

text: We only went here to see a movie at the Flagship Premium Cinemas Rutland. We had other commitments earlier in the day that precluded us from going to one of our local theaters, which had no showtimes later than 6:30pm for the movie we wanted to see. So, we drove an hour away, to Rutland. It's a great, scenic drive from bordering New Hampshire, a drive I have always enjoyed making. When we found the theater (having never been there before, nor having spent any time in Rutland previously, we looked around for a place to eat, near the theater at Rutland Plaza. We found a place about a block away, called Cara Mia's Pizza, and OMG! BEST pizza ever! Then we went to our movie. I just want to say that the Flagship Cinema in Rutland was AWESOME. My husband, a buttered popcorn addict, was delighted that they have a "self-serve buttering station". They had GREAT "combo deals" at the concessions. The theater itself was very nice, with amazingly comfortable chairs. We'll definitely be going back!

name: Dave's Adventures
text: We stopped here on a whim because we were hungry and heading through town. We were definitely not sorry we did. The restaurant doesn't look like much of a place from the road, however once you park there is a pleasant pond with seating overlooking it that is really nice. The interior was comfortable and clean. It had a bit of rustic and yet old world feel to it. The waitstaff was attentive and friendly. The food... well the food was outstanding. From appetizer to dessert we were thrilled with our selections. I would definitely stop here again when the opportunity presents itself.

name: Jennifer Curtis
text: Food was ok. Came out at all different times. So last people served were not happy. 15 min wait in between deliveries. Stay away from the chicken alfredo. The pizza was really good.

name: Jared Danowski-Harlow
text: I stopped by the Saturday before the Super Bowl after work. I personally know one person that works here and they said it was the busiest they've seen it all season. That being said, my friend didn't serve me or know I was there until after I paid and was about to leave, it was exceptional. The food came out real quick, drink service was excellent and the atmosphere was what I've come to expect. The owner was real nice, coming to talk to each table and single person at the bar to see how everything was. As a bonus I went to Italy two years ago and the food is second only to the real Italian in had then.

name: Cheyenne Olson
text: I love heading up to Jax! This is one of my favorite bars on the mountain. The atmosphere is more cozy then some of the other hot spots in Killington. They have great menu selections, as well as their late night menu. I highly recommend the mac and cheese bites! They almost always have live music playing a variety of genres. The prices on beverages are fair for the mountain. It can get crowded on the weekends and depending on the night they do have a cover charge. All of the bartenders are awesome, make sure you get a chance to meet KO! Hes the man and will truly make your experience at Jax one of a kind!

name: Lauren Wilder
text:
Went with 2 others. Very nice, enjoyable dinner. We had the spring rolls, both veggie and pork. Crispy on the outside, pork was a little dry, but dipping into the sweet chili sauce and a creamy sauce with jalapeno made it good. The veggie ones were reported as okay. Nothing special.
For our main meal, 2 of us had the cheese steak sandwich. They were big, served on a soft hoagie roll. We both felt that the filling was overcooked and dry. Again, saved by dipping into bleu cheese dressing that I had for my perfect side salad. The salad was fresh and appetizing. Onion petals were served with the other sandwich and were tasty. The 3rd sandwich was a grilled chicken breastbreast with guacamole, bacon, lettuce, tomato, onion and cheddar cheese on a grilled roll. The sandwich was wonderful. We all took half of our dinners home. They were quite large.
Our waitress was cheerful and helpful. She recently started working at Jax' and still is getting used to everything, but she is energetic and enthusiast and is doing a great job.
We will be back to try more of the menu, and watch tv on the big screen.

name: Tyler Lund
text: Jax doesn’t pretend to be anything it isn’t, which is a bit refreshing in Killington. It’s a bar and arcade above a laundromat. The beer selection is pretty good with several craft beers and local beer on tap. Beside the long bar, there isn’t a ton of space to sit. The arcade games are a nice touch though and a bit fun while enjoying a drink. The food is actually not bad as well, particularly the buffalo chicken quesadilla, which you get for free during happy hour if you order other food. We got this without realizing with our buffalo chicken nachos which were also good, though I preferred the quesadilla. The nachos had a little bit of a vinegar taste from the buffalo sauce. Service was friendly though not overly warm. Definitely a more relaxed vibe than many of the other bars around the area though

name: Jared Danowski-Harlow
text:
The Diamond Run Mall was once the thriving retail hub of the area but has since been on a steep decline, nothing of the management's fault but a stagnant economy in the area Having lost two of the three anchor stores, Sears and JC Penney, most of the smaller stores in the mall have closed up shop. Some chain stores are still in the mall like Victoria's Secret and GNC but others have left anticipating the closure of the mall, American Eagle and Eastern Mountain Sports to name a few. Even a local furniture store chain how took the old JC Penney space had to close.
Smaller locally owned stores have opened in their place with offer a great selection of stuff. The Mountain Man sells vinyl records new and used as well as band merch. The owner is a great guy who will order in any record you want if he can find it. Rutland Collectables is the go to place for any trading cards from Magic and Yu-Gi-Oh to sports cards of all kinds. He also has a nice selection of collectable coins. This is also the place to find used books at the best price in the whole city. In the defunct good court is now a play area for kids with bounce houses and toys in a safe smaller area of to the side. Their is a locally owned candy shop just a few store front down from there to satisfy your sweet tooth.
There is an Old Navy for sensible and affordable clothing options. Christopher and Banks for higher end clothing for adults. A hair salon and nail parlor for getting prettied up, and Bathworks for a home spa day afterwards. Two jewellery stores, Kay and Hannoush for plenty of options. Shoe Dept for all your footwear needs at great prices. Lastly a book, calendar and stationary store for gift ideas and personal needs.
There is a church that offers services multiple times a week at different times to accommodate any schedule.
If they could fill more stores in the mall, it would look a lot better but every few months another store bites the dust unfortunately. If the trend continues the mall can't sustain itself and will have to close, but this a refection of the economy of the area not mismanagement of the property.

name: Ryan Fisk
text:
Maybe it was the awesome Yelp reviews.  Maybe it was the eight hours of hard skiing that got our appetites worked up.  Maybe it was the euphoric air of wings and BBQ you could smell all the way down Okemo Mountain Road.  I'm not sure what it was, but we seemed to be hypnotically drawn to Tom's Loft Tavern for some après ski food and drink before heading back to NY.

My friend and I split an appetizer and two sandwiches, and had more food in front of us than we could have ever imagined.  The Thai Sticks are marinated in a curry sauce and grilled, served over lettuce with a chunky peanut sauce with just the right kick.  Sticks were juicy throughout...for grilled chicken, as good as it gets!

My friend ordered the pastrami reuben and I ordered the pulled pork sandwich.  Both were scrumptious, but her Reuben was definitely easier to pick up and eat, whereas mine was more of a fork and knife ordeal...thank goodness we grabbed utensils!  Thankfully, we ordered our food to go (shoutout to Jeremy for getting our order out quickly so we could catch a ski bus back to NY!), because this place was PACKED right after the slopes closed at 4pm.

As other reviewers have noted, Tom's loft is very cramped inside, with lots of corridors and not a single large open room.  The difference of 10-15 people on the main floor can transform this place from totally dead to completely jam-packed, so either go early and claim a table, or try to stop by during less busy times.  You can't fault such an old, quaint building for being so small and cozy, but be warned, this is not built for crowds like a base lodge or anything.

Despite all this, the food was sublime, and even though Okemo's on-mountain food options are pretty decent, I'm glad that we waited till we were off-mountain for our main meal...it was AWESOME!

The keilbasa and fried pickles were bland. It seemed to me that they had been breaded long before they were fried, they just didn't taste like pickles anymore. Even the coleslaw lacked flavor. I don't have much to say about the pulled pork or the Mac and cheese. The burnt ends though. Aside from the outer layer of burnt meat, it tasted and like it was roasted in a Crock-Pot. text: Deer Leap Trail to the overlook- amazing! The trail is well used and totally worth the trip. My kids and I hike it once a year, at least. With kids, usually takes about an hour and a half. name: Jt Amirault
text: We did an overnight on Bald Mountain on Jan 26 for our annual winter outing. Hiked up Bald Mountain Trail from Woodford Hollow up the Eastern slope. 2 miles in and 1,600 elevation gain to 2,800. Broke trail the whole way with snowshoes and full packs. Depth ranging 6 inches to near 3 feet and generally 1 to 2 feet. Hammocks kept us above the snow for sleeping. Underquilts and sleeping bags kept us warm with temps in upper single digits. Explored a bit behind the oak of Bald up the ridge trail and the balls maintain trail towards Bennington. We had planned to hike back down the West side to white rocks (4 miles), but, changed plans - one expedition member did not have snowshoes so we took the already broken trail. No signs of any other people. Great time had by all.

name: Patrick Fallon
text:
Carry in carry out. No facilities in winter. Very little cell coverage. This is not a place for the casual camper. Bring everything. Leave nothing. Take only 📷. One can get permits from the managing Ranger station for firewood harvesting and Christmas tree cutting. Small fees associated with harvesting.
There is a very small population of good solid mountain folk. Some sell firewood and may offer emergency help for the needy travelers. Slow speeds near the dwellings is appreciated. Approch local dwellings with extreme caution and be mindful of no trespass signage... Might be yer last mistake...

The vibrant colors of fall leaves are a tourist attraction. The winter snow season is loaded with sports. Mud season is slippery and the time to visit sugar shacks making fresh maple syrup. Sitting quickly followed by summer which usually is a bit more cool than lower elevations...

text: I have been to Lake Morey Resort for a few different conferences and have had a great experience each time! Such lovely views year round. It is just off I-91, easy to find, and has plenty of parking.

When foods are put out, it would be nice if they had gluten/dairy-free options. I know that the options has more to do with who is paying for it and what they requested, but even some signage as to what is actually IN the food on display would be really helpful. Other than that - everything has been stellar!

resp.text: Glad you enjoyed your day on the lake!  We'll have a larger fleet of Kicksparks to rent next winter!

text: This restaurant has a great variety of food at moderate prices. They make their own bread, and deep fried goodies are from scratch. We like their specially made root beer and black cherry soda. Great soups, sandwiches, salads. They also offer a variety of dinner selections, with daily specials. No breakfast items. They make their own vegetarian burger (not my favorite) for those who want that. Also note the interesting double hexagonal architecture of the building, which is used to create a very pleasant interior.

name: Robert J Blauvelt, Sr
text:
First time there.  What at amazing meal.  I had the seafood steamer pot which I've had in different places over the years.  Not many places can get this right with all the different seafood cooking times.  Served over fettuccini.  It was spot on perfect.  Very reasonable prices. My wife had wonderful mac and cheese.

This is certainly a destination when you come to Burlington. You can pay a non resident fee of $8 if you drive or you can rent a bike and enter for free.
There is a kayak and paddle board company that sets up in the northern part of the park.
The park offers trailer style camping as well.
The concession staff needs some more help and a better system to work with; they are hard working but could use some more help- many customers seemed agitated on a busy Saturday.
The beach is life guarded which is a plus...the rules are a bit more lax than we are used to at our local beach.
There is a playground and some barbecues available for use as well.
Enjoy your stay if you choose to go.

name: Sachin nayak
text:
Fairfield inn by Marriott Burlington was a pleasant stay. I stayed here for a couple of nights on the weekend. It was a good experience.

I had booked a couple of rooms for me and my friends. The rooms were clean. The queen beds were comfortable to sleep on. The room had a microwave and a small fridge. There was a coffee maker in the room with a couple of different flavors. I’d recommend to get coffee from the lobby downstairs since that was more delicious. The bathroom had a walk in style shower and the sink was outside the bathroom. The TV in my opinion needs a refresh. It was perfectly usable and had a few channels that they have subscribed but, a smart TV would’ve been better.

Due to this ongoing pandemic, the hotel had some services restricted like for example, breakfast. They had to-go boxes which had a fruit (apple/ orange) a bottle of water and a granola bar. They also had packed foods like milk, cereals and yogurt. The typical juices and coffee machines were all good and restocked from time to time.

The staff was super friendly and polite. The hotel had all the COVID precautions in place which was good to see. All the typical things that one expects from a Marriott branded hotel is all up to the mark.

resp.text: Hi Joanna:  The Bridge's name is the Creamery Bridge - because behind it - used to be a milk creamery.  You can still see one wall of the creamery when you pull into the parking lot behind the Creamery Bridge.  Most of the Covered Bridges in Vermont have names as well as numbers.  On this web page https://sites.google.com/site/vermontcobbleproject/covered-bridges you can see the picture of the old creamery, as well as find links the Vermont Covered Bridge Society and our National Registry Certificate - which state the Common Name of the Bridge as "Creamery Covered Bridge".  Thank you for the 4 stars!  JilMac - Brattleboro Garden Club - Creamery Covered Bridge park chairperson.

text: Our group of four made reservations at Cafe Provence just to be on the safe side.  Memorial day weekend can be a busy time in Brandon VT.  and it was!  We made it right on time at 12:00 noon and were greeted by the host.  Outdoor seating or inside seating was offered, we chose to be inside.  Our wait person was friendly and very professional.  She stated the specials and asked if we would like a refreshing drink.  We all selected our happiness and viewed the generous menu.  The "Brunch" menu can easily slip into an early dinner.  Our party ordered and had casual conversation. Without much time passing along came our dining pleasure.  Everything was prepared just perfect.  Not one compliant to be heard.  The portions met all if our desires.  Wonderful culinary skills on every dish presented at our table.  I might add the price was spot on.  Thanks Cafe Provence for a terrific dining experience.

text:
Red Clover Brewing has become one of our favorite spots. It's a bit of a drive from where we live, but it's worth it. This time, we opted to go have a couple of beers and then walk up to Cafe Provence for lunch. We're so glad we did.

The menu had switched to the bistro menu by the time we were ready for food. That's okay because between the specials and the bistro menu, it covered a lot. There are soups, salads, sandwiches, and a few other options.

The grilled steak sandwich with tobacco onions was fantastic. Fries are crisp and garlicky. Steak was seasoned well and I love tobacco onions. The bread it was on was awesome.

The burger was a little undercooked for one of the people in our party. He'd ordered medium rare and it came out rare. It was substantial in size, he said the bacon was cooked perfectly, and the taste of the burger was exceptional.

The other person in our party had one of the specials. At $14 it was a steal! It was two small salmon fillets that were grilled to perfection and served on a bed of lobster polenta.

Even with dessert and beers, our bill came to $74. That's impressive given the portions and quality/taste. We'll definitely go back!

text: 12/14/19 Been hearing advertisements for this place on the radio. It's a very quaint farm stand with the sweetest yellow lab that loves to greet everyone who enters. If you are in the area you need to check this place out. Fresh made pies and apple cider donuts.  We couldn't decide on one pie so we bought a pecan pie and a blueberry crumble. We had the blueberry crumble for dessert tonight. It was very good but so very different  from any other blueberry pie I have ever eaten. Who can resist fresh apple cider donuts? DEFINITELY NOT US! We bought a half dozen and ate a few on our ride home. And of course we had to have cold apple cider to go with our donuts. Looking forward to trying the Triple Berry pure fruit spread on toast tomorrow. There's so much more from fresh eggs to maple syrup, gift baskets, and veggies.  Debit/credit cards are accepted. The only negative thing about this place is that there is no public bathroom. I firmly  believe it is very bad business and just very wrong for any business to not have a bathroom available for their customers. I usually won't recommend patronizing any business that doesn't have a public bathroom. That's why I only give 4 stars.

Negatives -the walls are PAPER THIN. You can hear people talking in the next room over and the people above you just walk across their room and it sounds like an elephant upstairs . name: Johnny Azer
text: I have seen some phenomenal shows at this world class establishment. Probably one of the funnest gigs I have played in twenty years is when our band Sleeper Cell, got to warm up for The Samples. The crowd's enthuiasm was electric. I guess I need a following to play there. Hope I can get one soon. I still hear that killer crowd in my ears.

text: Where else are you going to go for good bands and decent prices? Also, you can listen to good music live while sipping at whiskey sours.

name: Stan Payne
text: I've only gone to two concerts at this venue in the past. The current location in South Burlington is a pretty small venue which is a former movie theater and oftentimes reaches maximum capacity. They do have decent craft beers on tap at the bars with appetizers on the menu. Most concert tickets are available at the box office directly from the venue when available. This venue is moving to a new location in the near future in the south end of Burlington and will be slightly bigger. For now, they are at the current location and I strongly recommend carpooling or taking public transportation because parking can be a nuisance. Please remember to drink responsibly and be considerate of other patrons.

text: Always a great place to see a show.  Small but big enough for a pit.  Two bars so you don't need to wait a long time for a drink and the staff are great!

name: Josh Harvey
text: Saw a couple shows here so far.  Pretty nice venue. I saw "Get The Lead Out" and "The Machine" both were great bands. I really enjoyed the experiences from both shows.  Higher Ground has a nice bar and a great selection of beers.

name: Cheyenne Olson
text: I have been to multiple events at higher ground and I have enjoyed each and everyone of them. The staff is friendly and helpful in times of need. They do have a coat check so I personally consider that an added bonus to any venue. The bar was equipped with fast acting bartenders who got what you needed in a timely manner. The security were all very professional but in a polite manner.  I have only been to standing only shows but the layout is fantastic for it. I imagine assigned seat shows would be equally enjoyable from any seat, as the stage is raised several feet from ground level. I'm unsure if they ever have any sort of food at this venue but they did not during my experiences at Higher Ground.

name: Eric Lane
text: Great venue with all kinds of good music acts year round.  Good times!

name: Liana Edwards
text: Great concert venue. There is a smaller, more intimate room and a larger room. Both have just standing space on the floor. Tickets are always super cheap even when really famous bands play! It's also a good place to hear smaller indie or local bands.
