text: So I just moved here from Wilmington North Carolina. My girlfriend and I tried to go here because we had tickets to see Coleman Hell. After getting there I showed them my North Carolina ID that shows that I'm clearly 21 years of age. They took my ID into the back away from me and we stood there for 15 minutes. I asked the guy at the door where my ID is and he stated she's was just doing here job, while he talked to me like I was a child... then he threatened to kick me out because I was getting an "attitude". She returned with my ID to tell me that she wouldn't  accept it because it wasn't real or even registered anywhere in the United States. I then showered her my old out of date ID that states the same information and she proceeded to take both IDs back to the back; so I stopped her and demanded my ID's back. She insisted she needed to take photo copies of them for "training" reasons. Next I was rudely asked to leave or I would be escorted out by the rude bouncer whom had been sizing me up the entire time. This experience was a waste of my time, and money. I will NEVER go back to this facility. Out of state people beware. I have been going to shows for years and never been treated the way I was here; therefore it is my right as a 21 year old American citizen to be able to drink anywhere that serves alcohol.

text: I love Panera. The food always tastes fresh and clean. The service was quick and the restaurant was clean. I ordered online and picked it up inside in 10 min. and everything was right. What's not to like? The bagels, baked goods, sandwiches, soups, salads, etc. are great and love being a repeat customer!  I definitely recommend to come and eat here.

name: Christopher Grizzle
text: Consistently excellent food and service. Have never been disappointed with a visit. Definitely one of my favorite places for a quality fast meal.

name: Bob Flaherty
text: Love the food but for some reason, this Panera location frequently messes up the order.  I usually try to keep the orders simple to avoid any issues. Didn't work today.  Ordered quantity 2 chicken soup bread bowls. Instead received 1 cup of chicken soup and 1 cup broccoli cheddar...  Paid to have chicken added to my Greek Salad and that was missing too.  I even tipped them well but to no avail.

name: John Martin
text: We attempted to order takeout from them we were asked every question except for my Social Security number including a complete spelling of my first and last name. After answering all the questions and getting our order in  (5 minutes later) we were told we couldn’t order unless we had a credit card but if we came and ordered there we could pay cash. I guess  if you don’t use a credit card don’t bother to call ahead  for takeout. We called five guys we were on the phone for about one minute and they’re going to have our order ready in five minutes. I work on Shelburne Road order lunch all over never had that experience. All the other restaurants are ok with us paying cash when we get there.  They may want to start off their conversation with a take out order do you have a credit card?

But man, I just wish that their food had some real flavor and that their bread was doughier instead of dry and tasteless. It's also really on the expensive side for sandwiches and such.

Total bill including tax and gratuity came to $ 26.  Easy to find, parking available, order online for pickup, kid and disability friendly, bathrooms onsite.

text: The food is standard Panera food. My issue is with their management team. I called about getting a refund on an order that my company pre-purchased for a Sunday, but on the day of the event, it needed to be cancelled. Cancelling the lunch order wasn't on anyone's radar, so I'm sure the order was made. When I called Panera to talk to someone about the possibility of at least getting the drinks/cookies refunded (these could be resold), I was told by Manager Joe that he would need to as his supervisor because the day of the order had already passed. He told me he would get back to me in a day or two. After a week without hearing from Joe, I called back and Joe was off, but explained to a different manager what Joe and I were working on, and she said that she would be sure to have Joe call me back the next day. Another two days go by and no call from Joe. So, I call again and speak to another manager who wouldn't even give Joe my message because Joe would probably be too busy to call me back, and suggested that I call back the next day when a district manager (or something like it) named Tyler would be there from 6am. I did not call Tyler, and I'm done trying to get any refund at all, but you can be sure that I won't make any more purchases at Panera on behalf of my company. And just to note, this was one of three lunch orders that we placed within about 10 days that all equaled up to about $600!

text: My second visit here! Only the scoop shop is open inside.. we got the maple walnut and the oatmeal cookie chunk.. great flavors only available at the factory! Don’t forget the flavor graveyard!!

name: Sachin nayak
text:
If you love ice cream or are an occasional ice cream eater, this is one of those go-to places. The ice cream is fresh, super delicious and you’d be spoilt for choices.

We visited this place during this ongoing pandemic and there a few changes. The factory tours are closed. There’s COVID precautions in place like face coverings and 6 feet distance while in the queue and there are these barcodes to help you look at the flavor offerings and order while you’re in the queue.

They have a ton of offerings from your typical ice cream to frozen yogurt, non dairy and sorbet. The flavors are delicious. There are two options- small(2 scoops) and large(3 scoops). There’s a ton to choose from and they are all fresh and flavorful. You’d be doing the ice cream a disservice if you don’t get the waffle cone with it. I had a party of 9 and we all had different flavors and they were all yum!

One more thing to note, once you’re done with your order and you get your ice cream, there’s no seating space for you to sit and eat. You’ll have to walk around and that’s what we did and we stumbled upon this ‘flavor graveyard’ which is just a few minutes away. You’d be able to pay respects to the discontinued flavors here :D You’d be surprised to see some of the flavors out there in the graveyard and who knows, you might stumble upon a flavor which you liked is now retired.

There’s lots of places to click photos around. I’d recommend this place to anyone who’s had eaten ice cream at least once in their life and give this place a try.

name: Julie Nielsen
text: They are doing a great job keeping everyone safe and socially distant. There are no tours of the factory but you can still get ice cream. There is a small souvenir stand outside. The 7 layer bar ice cream is delicious. I love coconut and there is plenty of that. Enjoy?

name: Gian Carlo
text: Can you love a place a little too much? Try the fresh made ice cream, especially flavors you can only find here! Do the tour too if you're a "how things work" nerd. Loved it! And the graveyard of retired ice cream flavors - a trip down memory lane. Ben and Jerry, 2 NY imports who improved the state immeasurably, just like brother Bernie!

name: Ellie Clevenstine
text: Always fabulous. Pricey, but creative flavors, huge servings, and friendly staff.

name: Cassy Janes
text: The factory wasn't open for tours because of covid stuff of course but they had a display out of all the giftshop stuff and you could tell them what you wanted and pay for it at the icecream counter. The icecream was amazing!! So rich, fresh, and creamy... even better than getting it from the store. The staff was friendly, courteous and so helpful. Counter surfaces were sanitized immediately  between each customer. They moved us quickly but didn't make us feel rushed.

name: Nick Arduini
text: Living in Vermont we still enjoy visiting Ben and Jerry's at least once a year, its definitely worth the visit, although it can be pretty busy on weekends. Be sure to take the factory and tour, where you can sample a flavor not available in stores.

name: Amanda Broseus
text:
Such a great stop during our time in Vermont! Loved learning of the ice cream making process, especially as a quality engineer in the food industry who totally geeks out over that stuff. Very clean facility, good company values, and great tasting ice cream samples. The tour doesn't last very long as it is a small facility, but it's a cheap tour and worth the price.

Cute little gift shop and flavor graveyard as well!

resp.text: Amanda - Thank you SO much for the fantastic review!!! We are happy to hear that you had a wonderful experience. Please come back and visit soon!

name: Anne-Margaret McElroy
text: Great family place with really good ice cream and though it is now owned and operated by Unilever it has still kept its original founders core ideas and sense of community. They give tours, offer ice cream making class and serve a variety of flavors. Lots of visuals, collectables, etc. Gift shop is small, there are stairs to climb or a path weather permitting, not for the faint of heart but there is a drop off and handicapped parking at the top of the drive. Bathrooms are small as well compared to the ratio of people that visit, plan accordingly in warmer weather. Four ice cream windows with two huge bay doors that open in warmer weather. My favorite part of B&J was the graveyard for retired flavors.

name: Frank Armento
text: We did a tour today on a Sunday very cool experience the tickets are $4 each and get a cool history and lesson on how their delicious ice cream is made. You get sample at the end. The tour guide was very funny always making a joke. You exit the tour to a gift shop with s bunch of cool items. As well the ice cream shop here is so delicious because its fresh. You can tell the difference. If your in Vermont definitely need to stop by here no matter how far you are. We drove 70 miles today to visit and it was worth it.

text: $4 tour for adults which lasted about 30 minutes and came with a generous (about a half scoop) sample. Be sure to check out the flavor graveyard, I couldn't believe some existed!

name: Brynn Casamassa
text: Currently, they aren't doing tours but the ice cream was great! The flavor graveyard was nostalgic, for true Ben and Jerry's fans.

name: Kate S.
text:
Went here late on a weekday very easy no lines but it's also off season and was cold and rainy! There's multiple levels of parking lots but they are all pretty muddy so plan to walk and not wear nice shoes
Had a great custom cone 👍👍

name: Bruce Monroe
text: A bit pricey. So be careful bringing the kiddies into the gift shop. Average t shirt is $24.00. No matter what size. Long aait for ice cream, 37 minutes today to get a waffle cone for $8.00 dollars. Wow!!!! Commercial much. Still fun though just dealing with sticker shock.

name: James
text:
I don't think that Ben and Jerry's needs to be explained, but you can't really go through Vermont without stopping at the factory. The tour was a little dull, I'm sure that they have a video of it online but if you made the trip you might as well do it.
The portion sizes are huge when you buy them and everyone working there is rather nice.

name: Robb Geesen
text:
They really need to reconsider the line situation.... waited in line for 40 minutes, in rain and cold wind blowing.
Perhaps the could set up individual to go cups of ice cream in advance and have an express line for just those..since looked like that is what most customers were buying.  Disappointed no tours due to covid.

name: Sean Williams
text: $4 tour for adults which lasted about 30 minutes and came with a generous (about a half scoop) sample. Be sure to check out the flavor graveyard, I couldn't believe some existed!

name: Adrian Evans
text:
Enjoyed the visit,short lines for the tour.
Mixed feeling about the place,they need to do healthier ice cream.

name: Tim McCann
text: It was fun and yummy but we were underwhelmed by the factory tour

name: Logan
text: Very cool factory with great ice cream. While the factory tour is very short and quick, it's well worth the small price ($4 per adult as of June 2017).

name: P B
text: Best ice creams hands down, if you have never been do the tour and visit the ice cream flavor graveyard.

name: Adrian Evans
text:
Enjoyed the visit,short lines for the tour.
Mixed feeling about the place,they need to do healthier ice cream.

name: Daniel Neuner
text: Delishious and safe. Lotsa tourists including myself

name: Avi Ghelman
text: The tour was nice, short but nice. I expected a bit more explanation about the process, but I assume this was nit feasible. Overall a nice place to visitefor a couple of hours

name: truetexas
text: Fun tour.....loveed it.

name: JG DeBiasio
text: Very touristy.  Busy with long waits.  Delicious ice cream and history.  It was a rainy day.

name: Gabrielle Bills
text: The tour is a great quick activity with a perfect amount of ice cream to taste at the end. Children under 12 are free, and outside the is a playground and plenty of space to run around. Fun and quirky, with the flavor graveyard and gift shop... I go at least a couple of times a year when we have visitors from out of town.

name: Mark LoGiurato
text: Fun place to visit with family - short tour, but don't miss the graveyard!

name: Sterling Magera
text: Just the best tour I've ever been on. Even the sample during the tour was bigger than expected. And the gift shop had some interesting stuff. Not to mention the ice-cream in their shop tasted better than any I've had before. Getting to the graveyard in the ice was tricky...

name: Tim McCann
text: It was fun and yummy but we were underwhelmed by the factory tour

name: Larry Gianakis
text: The new cereal ice cream was really good. Always a fun stop.  We didn't have time for the tour this time unfortunately.

name: Yoann Lussier
text: It brings back the kid in me everytime I set a foot inside this monument dedicated to making the best flavors in the world. Driving up to the factory, my mouth is already watering. Once inside, I have a flavor before entering the tour, their mini sample and another one on my way out. Keep at it, you make everyone a kid again.

name: M. Kaseweter
text: efficient and clean experience albeit incomplete (no tour, no samples, etc.) during COVID

name: Logan
text: Very cool factory with great ice cream. While the factory tour is very short and quick, it's well worth the small price ($4 per adult as of June 2017).

name: M.Evergreen
text:
Wow!! What a way to feel like a total kid again! Take the tour, it's 100% worth the $4 and you even get to sample a new flavor!! From the history of Been and Jerry themselves to the packaging and cooling rooms the tour had so much fascinating stuff to look at, I wanted to dive Right in and start working here.
Be sure to make your way over to the Flavor Graveyard to see some of your favorite retired flavors, the headstones are so funny!!
A great place to bring guests and visitors.

name: Daniel Neuner
text: Delishious and safe. Lotsa tourists including myself

name: Dave Hall
text: Ice cream... To bad the tour is shut down.

name: Jessica Lewis
text: This was such a fun place to visit. The tour was a bit short in my opinion but still enjoyed it and the ice cream sample at the end was delicious.

name: Allison B
text: Fun gift shop and (of course) lots of ice cream options. We didn't get to do the tour, as it was at least an hour wait, which is a long time for this type of stop (and it wasn't that busy). I'd still recommend a stop, even without the tour.

name: Alisa Belova
text: Ice cream was melted and also service was very slow

resp.text:
Hi Alisa,

Thank you for taking time to rate us. Very sorry to hear you did not have a good experience.  We would gladly refund your ice cream purchase if you email your mailing address to benjerrytour@gmail.com.  As well if you would like to share details we would appreciate learning more.

name: Viera Levitt
text: Great visit with the kids and adults. Tour starts with the video, Ice Cream sample at the end. Enjoyable. Staff was flexible and let us come in with the group that was just leaving.

resp.text: Viera - Thanks for the awesome review!! We are so happy to hear that you had a great time and hope that you will come back and visit again!

name: Thomas Lambert
text: The entire operation was a great learning experience. Definitely go during the off season; we went during the fall and there was hardly a wait. However, the parking lots are huge, indicating serious traffic during the peak season. At the end of the factory tour you get to taste Ice Cream that isn't released yet...we had Apple Pie. On the other side, they also have a graveyard of Ice Creams you can visit. It's some of the flavors they have discontinued. Thanks for the experience!

name: Matthew Hiserodt
text: We loved this place, but know that it gets insanely crowded so I would recommend going in the morning.  We got there 30 minutes after opening and got tickets for a tour right away.  By the time we left that was obviously no longer the case as they had filled up multiple parking lots.  Tour takes about 30 minutes with free ice cream sample at end and costs liek $4 for adults and I think kids were free (if i remember right).  Kids enjoyed doing tie dying and coloring outside and visiting the flavor graveyard.  We ended up being here for around 2 hours.   A must stop for families in the area.

resp.text: Matt - Thank you so much for the awesome review!! We totally recommend visiting in the early hours in the busy months too and are happy to hear you had such a fantastic experience! Thanks again!

name: Aaron Lyon
text:
Fun tour, Some free ice cream samples. Very busy on weekends and summer but manageable.
Love the flavor graveyard with all the old flavors)
Eat a Vermonster while you are there!

name: Sean Gauvreau
text: It's the Ben & Jerry's factory. What more do you want? A+++

name: Kyle Ledoux
text:
Nice place to stop by for a little taste of Vermont. The factory tours are pretty cool, and they run frequently. You can learn about the history of the company and how they make ice cream.
Grab a cone or bowl at the window and taste the goodness! Be warned, it's definitely tourist priced. $$$
There's a big playground to let the kids run around in, so sugar em up and let them tire themselves out!
Protip, visit the old flavor graveyard up on the hill to see all the B&J retired flavors in a mock cemetery.

name: jesse shaw
text: eh. Tourist Trap.  Maybe my own anticipation ruined my expectations of this place.  Maybe it was the poor guiding of vehicles mixing with pedestrians that led to stand still traffic inside the compound. Maybe it was the no air conditioning. Maybe it was the too many people for such a small inside space. Maybe it was the 30 minute wait for ice cream under the blaring sun.  Maybe it was the stale tasting ice cream. Just not what I expected from my favorite ice cream company.

name: Alan Walters
text: Well worth $4...free sample and brief history lesson, I would go back!

name: Anne Choyce
text: Love to visit here. A favorite for our family. The graveyard with retired ice cream flavors is cool. Of course, the best ice cream ever!

resp.text: Anne - Best. Ice Cream. Ever? WE AGREE!! Thank you so much for the review and please come back and visit us soon!

name: Garrison Parthemore
text: This place is freaking awesome. We were very surprised how affordable the tour was. ($4 for adults $3 for children) The first part of the tour is an informational video about the story of Ben and Jerry's. Next was a muezzin where the production of their ice cream was talked about.  The last part of the tour was a taste test, where they let us sample ice cream, and it was fantastic. Don't forget the free high fives! Our tour guides name was Will and he was fantastic. We can't emphasize how nice and knowledgeable Will was. The tour itself is pretty short which is good and then afterwards you can get something from the gift shop. If you really want to get the best experience, stop at the ice cream stand near the entrance for some fantastic ice cream. Could not recommend this more!

name: Laurie __
text: Great stop for some great ice cream!

name: Justin C
text: My kids had a fantastic time. The price is reasonable too! For the four of us, three adults and one child, it was 12 dollars. My kids seemed engaged and it was nice to get ice cream at the end.

name: Glenn Giles
text: See how great ice cream is made and a sample of a new flavor at the end of the tour.

name: Bardiya Akhbari
text: I really like this place. The tour is short and they don't go in detail about the process, but staffs are so awesome and happy. The ending with one scope of ice-cream is awesome too! This is a good 45 minutes stop on your way to Burlington or around that area.

name: Donald Mayotte
text: Really nice place to go with the family kids will have a blast there is a really nice playground outside and of course the ice cream is excellent. Go up and enjoy the tour check it out

resp.text: Donald - Thank you for the great review! Sounds like you got to explore the playground, in addition to the factory experience and we are glad you had a good time! Come back and visit soon!

name: Fly Fisherman
text: Interesting tour at a roadside attraction.  Very clean facilities. I rated the 4 due to the $4 tour fee. In my opinion there should be no charge. It's B&J's opportunity to sell is more ie cream

name: Vee
text: One item off my foodie bucket list! Did the factory tour & I definitely recommend it. The tour itself is not long and goes over the basics of how they make their ice cream. There is also a short political video message included in the tour, but it emphasizes the ongoing social advocacy Ben and Jerry's is known for. A nice sample is included at the end of the tour. There are also various other activities to do around the factory, including the flavor graveyard, children's playground and even making your own tie dyed shirt!

name: Thomas Thrift
text: Oh yeah!!! This is a must visit while in Vermont. Love the taste test.

name: Ankit Dhaniwala
text: Just the ice cream was good, nothing really great about the factory tour. The tour guide was funny though...

name: Micah Allen
text: They had 1 teller working a Friday, the line was to the parking lot.

resp.text: Thank you for taking the time to rate us. We apologize for your less than euphoric experience.  To maintain social distancing and eliminate touch points we've had to adjust our operation. We are trying to do what's best for our employees and our guests. If you would like to share more detail please mail benjerrytour@gmail.com.  We would appreciate learning more.

name: Kristy Mchenry
text: Ice cream is always awesome but to be honest, the tour isn't worth the (small amount of) money. You watch a short video you can probably find on Youtube and then look at a bunch of metal cans/tubes. You do get a sample at the end though. Also, we always just buy a pint because it's basically  same price as a cone! Definitely worth stopping by nonetheless!

text: Go see the graveyard....pay homage to those that are gone...then make your own tie dye shirt.

resp.text: Peter - Thank you so much for the awesome review!!

name: Kevin Murphy
text: The tour isn't very exciting, but it is inexpensive and something to do before eating ice cream. They show you a short film about the company. You get to see some of the retired flavors. You get to see the production floor from above. At the end, they let you sample a special flavor. They have a nice gift shop and an ice cream counter. The kids like the playground and a the graveyard for dead flavors.

name: Ruth Anderson
text: A real joy. And who knew you could enjoy it without actually eating ice cream.

resp.text: Ruth - Wow! Thanks for the stellar review!!

name: Ty McCarthy
text: Fun place. Great company

name: Jan Conway-Porcelli
text: Always a favorite!  If you are in Waterbury Vermont you have to just go for the tour and for the hundreds of different creative flavors of ice cream.  They have a playground outside and picnic tables, flowers and a grassy pasture to give the kids a way of releasing there energy.

name: Catherine Herlich
text:
A must go.  Be smart, have your ice cream for breakfast.  The line can be like the Long Island Expressway on a summer Friday going east.  Jammed.
So, don't have lunch!

name: Sher Woei Foon
text: Friendly and educational tour. Icecream graveyard is a must to visit. It bring back your memory.

name: Donald Mayotte
text: Really nice place to go with the family kids will have a blast there is a really nice playground outside and of course the ice cream is excellent. Go up and enjoy the tour check it out

resp.text: Donald - Thank you for the great review! Sounds like you got to explore the playground, in addition to the factory experience and we are glad you had a good time! Come back and visit soon!

name: Peter Carney
text: Awesome

resp.text: Peter - YA! So happy to hear! Thank you!

name: Larae Sams
text: Of course the ice cream was good.  I wish the tour was a little ....more.

name: Andrew Rollins
text: It's not going to wow you... you watch a history movie, then see some of the plant through some windows... and a baby size sample of ice cream.

name: Neal Brassard
text: The factory tour was very informative.

name: Ams
text: Who doesn't love Ben and Jerrys, must visit when in the neighborhood

name: Paul Lindsey
text: Was a very nice visit and factory tour. Free ice cream that Ben and Jerry's haven't made yet! The tour itself is okay. They go over the production and product lines in good detail. The gift shop is pretty good. I'd recommend visiting the flavor graveyard. There are a lot of flavors I'm surprised they even made.

name: Chris Mandragora
text: Fun tour...cost $7/person. Tour consisted of an animated documentary about the company and a short tour of the facilty with a small tasting of a new flavor at the end. Gift shop was super pricey but expected it to be. Ice cream was out of this world and tour guide was very good. Check it out.

name: Richard Davis
text: This thing was huge so much toppings made it were you couldn't really enjoy the icecream.

name: Patrick DeMarco
text: I loved everything about Ben & Jerry's........I have taken the tour 4 times !!  I love getting to taste the sample of the day..and more too..love the grounds all around Ben & Jerry's too !!  I will definitely come again and again !!

name: Aunt Psy
text: All in all pretty disappointing. A short tour where you just look at a bunch of pipes and vats.you get a small cup of ice cream at the end. PS, Ben and Jerry, there are other flavors in the world besides chocolate.

resp.text: Thank you for taking the time to let us know about your visit. Sorry we missed the mark of your expectations.  If you would like to share more please email benjerrytour@gmail.com. We would appreciate learning more.

name: Christopher Chanowitz
text: Awesome place friendly staff and great tour........and ICE CREAM

name: iTravel
text: Neat little museum. Yummy ice cream!

name: Jennifer Raymond
text: Go one the tour! It's like $5 and you can see the inside of the factory and you get a sample of ice cream!

name: H D
text: Great place to tour. Good tasting icecream

name: Robert Yarnall
text: Had a great visit with the kids. Did not wait long for our tour and of course the ice cream at the end was awesome.

name: Chris Bigg
text: Fun little tour.  Random employee handed me a sundae she just made and it was delicious.  The tour had a short video and then you got to see the production floor.  Its making ice cream I didn't expect unicorns to magically appear. Then you were given a sample.  It cost $4 and was worth every penny.  There is a little playground in the back for kids, and the hidden flavor graveyard out back which was kind of fun.

name: Rick Valenta
text: A great place to take the kids or friends from out of town.  The ice cream is as good as it gets.  Lots of things to do around the property besides the tour, including a play ground, ice cream flavor graveyard, a few photo op areas, and a gift shop.  A good stop in for tourists and locals alike.

name: C Seaver
text: Great tour.  It was fun learning about the humble beginnings of one of my favorite icecream companies. If your in Vermont worth a stop

name: Chris Bigg
text: Fun little tour.  Random employee handed me a sundae she just made and it was delicious.  The tour had a short video and then you got to see the production floor.  Its making ice cream I didn't expect unicorns to magically appear. Then you were given a sample.  It cost $4 and was worth every penny.  There is a little playground in the back for kids, and the hidden flavor graveyard out back which was kind of fun.

name: Henry Hernandez
text: Great day trip!  We loved learning about Ben & Jerry's history and absolutely LOVED the segment calling for action by all of us to fight poverty and social injustice around the world!  Ben & Jerry's just got MORE awesome for us!  ☮️, ❤️and ICE CREAM!

name: Christopher H
text: Tourist trap for New Englanders. Better ice cream otherwise is found elsewhere in the state.

resp.text: Christopher - We are so sorry to hear that you did not enjoy your visit. Please feel free to message us at benjerrytour@gmail.com. We'd love to hear your feedback on how we can better improve our experience! Thank you.

name: Oliver Ames
text: It's the famous Ben & Jerry's! This is the original factory, and to learn more, I recommend taking the fantastic tour. At the end, you get to sample new flavors the company is trying out! The gift shop is nice and the ice cream speaks for itself. My favorite is coffee coffee buzz buzz buzz shake!

name: John Holzinger
text: The best Sundays

name: Andrew Evans
text: Highly recommend you stop by. A visit to B&J is simply a requirement you won't regret.

name: Megan R
text: Quick tour ending in a sample. Very charming, and a great stop if you're in the area. Be aware that some days you can't see the production because they are cleaning the tanks, still worth a look.

name: Stephanie Nickles
text: fun tour, it's only 1 room after the video theater room, so its quick. the line for ice cream was 1+ hour long which (for having all lanes open) was a bit extreme. good ice cream though, and nice gift shop. take the 5 minutes to visit the graveyard out back.

name: Winna Heilman
text: Visited the factory on a tour with my Girl Scout Reunion friends. It was amazing with wonderful Ice  cream afterwards.

name: Henry Hernandez
text: Great day trip!  We loved learning about Ben & Jerry's history and absolutely LOVED the segment calling for action by all of us to fight poverty and social injustice around the world!  Ben & Jerry's just got MORE awesome for us!  ☮️, ❤️and ICE CREAM!

name: Jim Carlins
text: The factory tour was an awesome event. Reasonably priced, informative and generous sampling of ice cream at the end.

resp.text: Jim - Thanks for the awesome review! We are so happy you enjoyed your visit!

name: Josef & Cindy Martin
text: Always like a little happiness!

name: Annie
text: Love the rice cream however their prices are very pricey ice cream for ice cream cakes

name: Ronald Hewett
text: Great place to go for ice cream and take a tour. If you like crowds and waiting this is the place for you. Good Luck have fun

name: Eliana Cañas Parra
text: Very fun place for this iconic ice-cream

name: T L
text: Fun little tour with a free sample at the end. Only $4.00 for adults and free for children under 12. Also sounds like a fun place to go on April Fools.

resp.text: Thanks for taking time to let us know about your visit.  April 1 this year brings Whiskey Pickle ice cream to the tour sample. Even better April 9th is Free Cone Day worldwide. Pace yourself and enjoy!

name: Kaku Global
text: I scream You scream We all scream for ice cream. Visit here if you are in Vermont! Good place, perfect for Summer days!

name: Mohammed Zafar
text: Ben & Jerry's has some of the best icecream. All their flavors are hard to beat. This being their factory outlet, they serve other flavors that aren't available outside of Vermont. The founders & brand stand for equality & social justice & this is put across in their intro video & posters onsite. Their factory tour was good but short

name: Jody Blanchard
text: Great day! I loved the set up and it was a great place to be for patents who cannot ordinarily afford to do this with their children. Great job Ben and Jerry's and many thanks to the vendors!

name: Bryce Caster
text: Overrated. While the flavor graveyard is fun, the tour is too short to be informative. I really wish it was about 15 minutes longer. Also, the lines are absurd. If you go, make sure to arrive early because tours usually sell out.

name: Jessica Mankowski
text: Didn't disappoint! The factory tour was fun.

name: Justin C
text: My kids had a fantastic time. The price is reasonable too! For the four of us, three adults and one child, it was 12 dollars. My kids seemed engaged and it was nice to get ice cream at the end.

name: Joanna Desaubies
text: My kids love our visits to Ben & Jerry's. Play at the playground, enjoy delicious ice cream and sometimes seeing the cows. They have great merchandise and affordable short tours inside the factory.

name: Molly Maroney
text: 30 minute your with free ice cream. A great stop on the tour of VT

name: Kristina Gallagher
text: Awesome family day learning the history of this amazing ice cream company from lil oke Vermont

name: Thomas Isidean
text: Must do tour in Vermont. It's a quick 20 minute tour. Great to learn about the history of this iconic business. The free sample at the end is a bonus. Nice gift shop for souvenirs.

name: T S
text: Just ok.  Long lines.  Can get same Ice Cream much cheaper in stores

resp.text: Thanks for taking time to write about your visit.  Sorry to hear we didn't meet your expectations.  We would appreciate knowing more if you would like to contact us at benjerrytour@gmail.com.  Your feedback would be helpful.

name: john costello
text: Great playground, good service. Very friendly employees.

name: Matt Morris
text: Great staff who keep the tour moving in a very entertaining manner by cracking jokes and dispensing interesting nuggets of information. The tour was surprisingly short but it was really interesting. If you can maybe call ahead or arrange your visit to find out if the factory will be in full operation, you'll get the most out of it. Good fun for all the family.

name: Adi
text: Great place - only $4

name: Sandy Indy
text: Lots to do and see.  Lots of stops and gyms for Pogo..

name: Jason Hao
text: The tour is okay, but the sample awaiting you at the end is great. They have ice cream flavors here that aren't available elsewhere. Be sure to take a short walk to the flavor graveyard.

name: J. W.
text: Wish they had cows...would have made it more entertaining.  Tour was pretty boring. Did appreciate the free ice cream sample, but not sure what all the hype is about. Couldn't imagine going over the summer to wait in line.

name: Abbey LaMay-West
text: Always a bit crowded for my taste, but they do a pretty good job of handling the masses. Of course the ice cream is amazing. The tour is fun, but not spectacular - definitely a bucket list item, but not blown away.

name: Jayita Barua
text: A femto version of Willy Wonka's chocolate factory!

name: Robert Fischer
text: Can't beat the flavors. Delicious!

resp.text: Robert - We totally agree! Thank you for the fantastic review!

name: Andrew Patteson
text: It's Ben & Jerry's ice cream, why would you not stop here?! Delicious! Tour was hokey but good cheap fun. We were here in winter, so can't comment on the outdoor stuff. Pose for pics and eat ice cream, enjoy!

name: J. W.
text: Wish they had cows...would have made it more entertaining.  Tour was pretty boring. Did appreciate the free ice cream sample, but not sure what all the hype is about. Couldn't imagine going over the summer to wait in line.

name: Adi
text: Great place - only $4

name: Ron Monroe
text: Great family experience...  And ice cream to boot!

name: Theory of Bang
text: Pretty fun.

name: Scott Morris
text: So awesome! Been coming here for 20 years and will never stop. Mostly get the ice cream these days, but love the experience!

name: Matt Ronco
text: Chocolate therapy milkshake is cheaper than real therapy and tastes much better.

name: Brian Clarkson
text: Tour is ok, Not amazing . Ice cream is definitely amazing .

name: J Lewis
text: Can't say anything bad about Ben and Jerry's. Best ice cream.  Ever.  Great service, tours, and gifts as well!!!

name: Ginger Kelly
text: We went here to get ice cream. I thought it was ok for folks who want commercial-type entertainment. We prefer less commercial, more home-spun type adventures. Most folks were taking tours.  We  did not want to tour and get packed in a little space like sardenes in a can. The line for ice cream was way too long and the ice cream was outrageously expensive.  I couldn't taste the ice cream flavors through the super sweet waffle cone. All in all, I'm so glad we found an ice cream place. That's about it for Ben and Jerry's.

name: Josh Harris
text: Factory tours. Great ice cream and all the flavors in one spot. Friendly staff. What is there not to like?

name: Jazzie Red
text: I mean it's Ben and Jerry's ice....  Yummy!

resp.text: Jazzie - We agree!! Thank you for the fantastic review!

name: Cody Mix
text: Tourist trap at its finest. There is little to do and see here other than wait in excruciatingly long lines for ice cream (which could be purchased at most convenience stores in town) and go on a factory tour. The playground is run down and generally overcrowded on most days. Not a pleasant experience during the busy season.

name: Don Pettit
text: Informative tour. Sample was great

name: James Coric
text: Was a nice trip with the family. Just wish there was no political mombo jombo injected into the tour. Other then that ice cream is delicious and was fun

name: Patty Coulombe
text: Tour was fun, ice cream Delicious!

name: Mark Spangler
text: Very nice tour but could habe done workout the "political" ads in the movie on the tour..

name: Hazel Kidder
text: Great and informative tour! A quick tour and fun to do with the kids! Plus the ice cream is so good!

name: Michael Glynn
text: Love comming here. Second time here. Always good with family.

name: Ryan Marshall
text: Loved every minute of this place, the tour was very informative and the sample at the end was awesome, the cemetary for died flavors and the all around atmosphere, couldnt wait to find the limited edition gimme smores at my local market, will be going back again when in the area.

name: Jackie S Yoon
text:
I had PB double chocolate in the plain waffle.
I liked because it is a kind of chewy and good sweet. Waffles tasted crispy and freshy.
I didn't take its tour but it is worth to visit and have a scoop of icecream because of its taste and wide open nature view.  I had a great time.
Fyi, restroom is outside.

name: Elliot Schwartz
text: Fun tour includes a short movie, a look at the manufacturing for from above, and a sample of ice cream. Make sure to get tickets as soon as you arrive since it can be a wait until your tour time. They also have a playground, art activities, a food truck, gift shop, and ice cream shop.

name: Jackie S Yoon
text:

text:
Nice! B&J's offers a very pleasant "ra ra ra" tour of thier Waterbury factory followed by a tasting kitchen sampling. Maybe a bit brief and sort of functional from some perspectives.

Although they give tours seven days a week, year round (except for a couple holidays), if you want to see the factory floor in actual use as they manufacture and package ice cream, don't come on a weekend, and also call ahead to make sure they're not in the middle of the regular mandatory cleaning cycles when you'll be there. (Also, to ensure you get to try the best flavors, don't come on April Fool's day: this year's offering was Broccoli Cheddar Crunch!)

name: Jess Mallory
text: A wonderful and pristine place to camp with your family. It's very well laid out and the restroom facilitys are kept clean. You can buy firewood on the grounds and the staff are very helpful. The beach area and the boat launch areas are very good. Just a caution to family's with young children. Recomend you stay away from section A,  cliff area as there is a steep 75 ft drop to the reservoir at these campsites. Ask at the front gate when you check in.

FYI, It does take awhile to get to this park from the main road even though it is only 3 miles off it, it’s mostly a dirt road.

name: Mike Dover
text: The nicest state campground we have been to, comparing to many midwest and Colorado sites. Beautiful fall views of the lake or even the interior forest areas. Sites are separated from each other. Bathroom was close and clean and available. Hiking to historic farming sites was very good. Mountain biking single track flow routes were outstanding. Also the lake is big and beautiful and there is a swimming beach as well as a place to launch your own small water craft.  Close to town so a good option if you want to eat out a lot.

name: Steve Davidson
text: Waterbury Reservoir is spectacular year round. The New boat launch is going to really improve access to the lake from the dam side. Superb views, calm waters, and remote campsites all over.

name: Steve fox
text:
Little River State Park is near Waterbury, Vermont. I checked this place out when the State had a " free state park weekend", (no charge to enter for the day). So I went in with my bike and rode the mountain bike trails. access is from the "History Hike" trailhead.(you get a map when you enter the park).
I took Stonewall trail up the side of the mountain to Bear Lane, took a side trip out and back on Ricker Farm trail(this was a mistake, but what a nice trail! I recommend it anyway). then hook back up with the Dalley Loop trail (big doubletrack for the hikers) up a short ways to Hillfarmer. This brings you down the trail to Highbridge, which is the whole point of your ride: This trail is amazing. A Monster downhill flow trail with sexy curved berm turns, twists and turns all the way back to Dalley Loop and the parking lot. This ride may be done a few different ways, but this is the way I did it.
If you really want to  re-enact my day, then be sure to stop in after your ride at Stone Corral in Richmond Vt. afterwards for a fine beer and lunch. Excellent plan.

We will now plan this trip including a meal at 3 Squares Cafe.

text: Had my first experience at 3 Squares, and it was lovely.  Cozy, inviting space, very friendly service and the buttermilk fried chicken sandwich was generous in portion and flavor.  Highly recommend!

name: Elise Shanbacker
text: Great local spot for breakfast, lunch or casual dinner. Order at the counter and they bring it to your table. For breakfast, 3 squares excels in the French toast and pancake department, and they serve breakfast till 3. Pretty sure this is the only real breakfast spot in town; some other places only do brunch on weekends from about 10:30 on so for early birds 3 squares is the answer. The coffee is also good here.  They make a great sandwich, soup or salad for lunch. If you order something on focaccia, prepare for it to be very thick cut. For dinner, try the fennel sausage pasta in a tomato cream sauce; it is delicious. They also have a dessert case and beer (bottles/cans) and wine.

name: Mark Otte
text: This is a charming Cafe in little downtown Vergennes, Vermont. We enjoyed our meal of a delicious hamburger and their fries... In a cute setting. A variety of eclectic things on the menu and well-prepared. My only warning is it is not inexpensive, so if you've got a bunch of children you might want to rethink it?

name: Nancy Kierstead
text:
Lots to do here! And the scenery in central, northern Vermont is stunning! We used the pool and the hot tub, rented segways to tool around in the woods, ate lots of food... All the good stuff. I found the staff to be super helpful and friendly. Our unit was clean and spacious and very quiet.
(For the record I will never, EVER ride a Segway again... but maybe that's just me, lol. The rental people were very helpful and sent a couple of staff to rescue me - one gave me a ride back in the golf cart and the other rode my Segway back for me. And the details of the fiasco do make for a pretty funny little story. You should try riding one too!)

resp.text: Thank you for the five-star review of Smuggs, Nancy! We are very glad to hear you enjoyed your time at Smuggs and also have a funny story to pass on!

text: Beautiful place. Fun amenities!

resp.text: Thank you for your five-star review of Smugglers' Notch Resort, Max! We very much appreciate the positive feedback and hope to have you back soon at Smuggs!!

text: Smuggs love

name: Joseph Cincotta
text: Smugg's is a great place for all family members.  For kids from tots to teens.  A big hit for them is Fun Zone 2.0.  That's when they are not snowboarding or skiing on the slopes. For adults, there is of course,  great slopeside activities. And my favorite Snowshoeing on the trails, from beginner to ad too advanced, or going a little off trail, but take care.  There are great places to eat within Smugg's.   Shuttle buses may it easier to get around the resort, without cleaning off your car.  The shuttle even goes to a pub outside of the resort.  It's almost impossible to list every thing there is to. Thursday's end off with a mountain side fireworks display.  This Christmas to New Year's week was cold with temps almost getting out of negative numbers, but that didn't seem to stop anybody from having a super great time.

resp.text: Thank you for the amazing review, Joseph!  We are thrilled to hear you and the whole family took full advantage of everything Smuggs has to offer.

name: Adam Gomes
text: This time we stayed in Evergreen. I've been coming here for years, and my wife and I try to get up here at least every other year. It's a fantastic resort, and it's a wonderful place to stay any time of year. Obviously, if you ski / snowboard this is an excellent place to stay in the winter. But It's amazing all year long, and being relatively centrally located in the state, it's a short drive from all the big tourist spots in Vermont. The staff is always helpful and friendly, the views are stunning, and the rooms / condos are always clean and comfortable. I absolutely love Smuggs, and I plan on continuing to visit for years to come.

resp.text: Thank you for your five-star rating of Smuggs, Adam! We are very glad to hear that you have been a long time Smuggler and really appreciate the positive feedback regarding the amenities, staff, and scenery. We look forward to having you back soon!!

name: Janet Winey
text: This popular ski and summer resort is a great base for viewing the beautiful fall colors. An easy drive to Stowe, Burlington,  picturesque villages and covered bridges. Accommodations are well equipped condos with kitchens from studio to 3 bedroom in buildings perched on the mountainside.  Well known for great ski program and family fun. Guests with mobility issues may have  difficulty with uneven terrain and not all buildings have  elevators. Two restaurants on site and a Fun Zone for kids. No main gathering building. Activities during high season; limited schedule off season.

name: Valerie Duffy
text: This is a great place for family and outdoor activities.  A resort situated in upper Vermont within the green mountain splendor.  In the summer, you can drive from Stowe through the notch, which is glorious. The condos are very comfortable and well made. The kitchen is stocked with utensils, pots, pans, etc, which makes cooking a breeze (unless that is not what you like to do).  There are plenty of grills available too for outdoor cooking.  There are activities for everyone from terrific camps for children, hiking and walks for the more elite hiker to one who wants a low impact nature walk. There are a number of heated pools with all levels of slides.  There are loads of activities from a high intensity stretch an go, tennis, mountain biking, etc.  There is a convenience  store for supplies and fun local products.  There is all kinds of night time activities for the family, teens and adults.  The local area is terrific too for dining, outdoor activities, locally grown, etc, etc.  Pricy but worth it!

resp.text: Thank you for your five-star review of Smugglers' Notch Resort, Valerie!

text: I took my kids to the Fun Zone 2.0 at Smuggler's Notch and we had a great time. There's quite a bit to do for all ages, the only reason I didn't give a 5-star review is because the fun zone is split into three sections and all three sections you have to pay a different price. And all three sections are for specific age groups window when I asked them if that was the case they adamantly denied it but going through all three sections I know for a fact that the top floor is for the younger kids the bottom floor is for the older kids or the teenagers or the kids at heart Like Me common the third area is arcade for everybody

name: SGTB .William
text: Beautiful environment with big long trails and friendly people.  Fast lifts get you up the mountain with the option to exit half way up for novices.  True beginners have plenty of room to learn and the top of the mountain has trails and glades to offer intermediate to experts all of the fun and challenges they want plus an easy way down for those ready to hit the top for the first time.  Good food and drink for families and at the pub.  Friendly staff tops it all off keeping everything fun, safe, and clean.

name: Thomas Straffi
text: Wish I could give this place a better review as there are so many positives to mention. For example, the kids ski and snowboard programs are top notch, truly an excellent experience, and the advanced skiing terrain is classic New England,  challenging, narrow, steep trails. But the lift service is so frustrating that it takes away many of the positives and creates a level of frustration so that you focus on the negative. Only slow, double chairs!!???!! Com'on. You wait, and wait and wait for a chair. And if it's really cold and/or windy, be prepared for a long, slow, bone chilling lift ride to the top.

name: Liz Jones
text: Nice but more rustic than we expected

name: Matthew Hahn
text: Smuggs is a wonderful place for family. The activities are endless and the Hearth and Candle is a phenomenal restaurant. My only gripes with the resort is that the Evergreens could use an update similar to the look of the Aspens (love those rooms!) Also, my wife has been coming to this resort since she was a child and we wanted to get married here. Unfortunately, no one was really accommodating, so we had to go up to Jay Peak which focusing on weddings and has the manpower and tools to handle them. Lastly, as a married couple, bring back couples game night! It was one of our favorite activities!

name: Gordon Sims
text: Called 4 times during the week about their Daycation tickets and to check status. Was told tubing is on but not likely ice skating. Drive an hour the next day to be told rudely that tubing was cancelled. Still curious if we could use the pools etc and have a day with the kids, kept asking people about it and after talking to the 3rd rude person decided it wasn't worth dealing with these people and left. Won't likely ever go back here.

resp.text: Hi Gordon, we are sorry to hear about your Daycation experience. Please keep in mind all activities are weather dependent at the resort and apologize for tubing not being available.  We'd like to offer you another chance to use our Daycation pass at your leisure. Please call 1-800-523-2754 to schedule another time to visit. Thanks!

name: THE Vindaloo King
text:
Awesome.  My 2nd home in St. J.   I may have been 30 times. Maybe 50?  Service, food, hospitality are all tops. BYOB on the DIPA.
I'm stingy with 5-stars but they deserve it.

name: Nancy Kierstead
text: Between the three of us we had the red curry, the green curry, and the yellow curry. We were like a traffic light, LOL! Of course we all three sampled each others, all three were very good. My favorite was the red curry, just a little bit of heat. The yellow was a little more sweet. Had some coconut ice cream for dessert, very tasty also.

name: ANGELA BERUBE
text:
GREAT FOOD & FAMILY OWNED!!
DEFINITELY WORTH YOUR MONEY IF YOUR IN THE AREA STOP BY YOU WILL NOT BE DISAPPOINTED!
FYI when eating here you may want to were loose or stretchy pants cause your going to need extra belly room.

name: Jeffrey Barret
text: Be careful, if you order 'medium' its gonna be very spicy.

name: Daniel Morse
text: Red curry.  Get.. the .. red.. curry.  I wish I knew this when I went the first few times.  It wasn’t until I went there for lunch, and heard every single person around me order the red curry, that I finally knew what was up.  It’s the best, and kinda addictive.  And if you order the lunch special, you get to pick your main dish and get a couple egg rolls and crab Rangoon. Also comes with a small soup.  That and a Thai iced tea and you are all set.  No need to go back to work, your life is complete.

name: Tom J
text: We ordered four appetizers which were ok - chicken wings, steamed dumplings, fried tofu and fourth one was disappointing (fresh spring rolls).

name: Cyndy Andrews
text:
Off the chain delicious Thai food at a great price! Everything we've had has been wonderful.

The staff is great, the restaurant is warm and inviting and the take out is just as good!

name: Julia McKinley
text: The best Thai restaurant. Plus, their wait staff are the most pleasant people.

name: Chantal Mehanna
text: All the food here is amazing!  A few of my favorites are the Pad Thai, Thai noodle soup, tom-kha with tofu, fresh spring rolls, sweet & sour with chicken and the best crab rangoons / Thai iced tea I've ever had!  The staff is very kind and always a pleasure to visit. I recommend this restaurant to all my friends and family.

text: I liked this place. Honestly though, I've liked every Thai restaurant I've eaten at and they've all had basically the same menu. The pineapple in the panang curry was a nice touch and the protein options were  bit more diverse than other similar places I've visited. In addition to the standard chicken, beef, shrimp and tofu you expect, they also served squid, scallops, and fish in their dishes.
