text: I cannot rate them high enough. Always hot, fresh and worth a trip, for their crab rangoons alone. They can get pretty busy, but it's worth the wait. One of the best Thai restaurants I've been to.

name: Kyle Butler
text: Dined in. Picked out the chicken pad thai, and my girlfriend picked up the drunken noodle with crab rangoons as the appetizer. The food was great, but the service was poor. The young lady didn't seem to care too much about quality service, and barely said 2 words to us after we received our meals. Just very cold. But again, the food was stellar.

name: Jonathan Forrest
text: The food is always phenomenal and the service is impeccable. I feel more than welcome here.

name: Cheyenne Ruggles
text:
THe food was great. ordered take out online and picked it up. The waitress loudly argued with someone in the back while I waited for food to be brought out, creating an awkward and uncomfortable atmosphere. Had I not taken the food out of the bag to sort it, the ordered soup would have spilled all over my truck.

Hesitant to return due to this experience

name: Chris Bergen
text: We come here all the time and the food is incredible. The service is too!!!

name: Alexander Brown
text: Amazing food and really great staff

name: Joseph Kennedy
text: Totally lacks authenticity. Frozen vegetables in most every dish. Prices are too high. Sure a few local friends and family members submit their biased reviews. Want to try great Thai in Vermont? Try the Royal Orchid in Montpelier....AWESOME!

name: Greg Schoppe
text: Fantastic Thai, in the least expected location. The entire menu is delicious and very affordable.

name: Jeanne Segretto Miller
text: Cozy atmosphere and great food

name: Sarah Boucher
text: Delicious food! Good prices. Great for a date.

name: John Evans
text: The food was great. There appeared to be only one waitress so the service to check out was a bit slow.

name: Mike carlisle
text: Great food! Fresh and well-made. Attentive and friendly staff.

name: keith whitcomb sr
text: Good food small portions

name: Carl Acker
text: This is one of the best restaurants in the area. They have a excellent lunch special.

name: Heather Stone
text: Awesome food large portion

name: Elliott Feulner
text: Excellent curries,  good portions, affordable price,  and really friendly staff

name: Katherine Yoder
text: I dream of the Thai Lad Nar and Tom Kha. Great service, well-portioned, excellent food.

name: Ann Moore
text: Great place for  mid afternoon.

name: Austin Perdue
text: Good food, fast service, weak English but got my order right.

name: Nancy McBey
text: Great food, good service!

name: Joanna Hayes
text: We love the food at Kham's.  The service is great too!

name: Jerre Hoffman
text: Great Thai food good service

name: CacheCoder
text: Love the place, great food, quite atmosphere

name: Jeremy Hodge
text: Great food!

name: Desiree Hawkins
text: my favorite food

name: Helen Paquin
text: Delicious food!

name: Tammy Ross-Smith
text: Good lunch specials.

name: frances ellis
text: Favorite place to eat in St. J

name: Marcus B
text: Awesome Thai food.

name: jessica Sanville
text: The food is great

name: william barry
text: Awesome Thai food

name: Kevin Gallagher
text: Bestist and only-est Thai food in the NEK

name: Matthew Prohaska
text: Great food in St Johnsbury

name: Lj Stewart
text: Very good Thai food

name: Brian Duda
text: Great Thai food

name: Ryan Schwartz
text: Tasty Thai food!

name: Real Thibeault
text:
(Translated by Google) I am a regular at Thai restaurants and this one did not impress me. The food is very good and the service pretty good. I would go back from time to time if I lived nearby, but I would not do 100km just to eat there.

(Original)
Je suis un habitué des restaurants Thaï et celui-ci ne m'as pas impressionné. La nourriture est très bonne et le service plutôt bon. J'y retournerais de temps en temps si j'habitais proche, mais je ne ferais pas 100km juste pour aller manger là.

name: Keanu Von Diez
text: The default Grocery store and market of Burlington and the UVM campus. As alright as it gets. Good selection of products, decent customer service; however be prepared to pay for the added convenience and for the added cost of healthy or prepared food... For inexpensive bulk & ingredients go to the larger grocery stores or local ethnic markets. Relatively good for small items or the odd purchase

resp.text: Hi Keanu - If there's something we could have done during your visit to improve the 3-star rating to a 5-star rating, feel free to be in touch! - Allison (ahope@citymarket.coop)

name: Linda LeCompte
text: Good healthy options in all departments. Very good store made foods. I balance this store with a traditional supermarket for certain items. Prices are higher here than the traditional supermarket for same items. I definitely couldn't live without City Market, though.

resp.text: Hi Linda, thanks so much for this kind review and feedback! I did want to make sure you knew about our Co-op Basics program. This is a line of everyday low price items with over 350 items on the list: https://www.citymarket.coop/basics! Let us know if you have further feedback at info@citymarket.coop and thanks for your support!

name: bluwasaabi
text: They have reverse osmosis filtered water I need. I enjoy shopping here but it's too far away to be my regular store.

resp.text: Thanks for the review! Glad you're able to get your RO water filled up at the Co-op!

name: Johnny Azer
text: I am glad it turned out they were only closed for a day, I assumed it was a week and missed them for fair prices and selections. They have all types of meat and goodies from A to Z. Would be great if they carry rabbit food..pellets, but otherwise I like all the goodies that are affordable only a decent walk from my house.

resp.text: Hi Johnny, thanks for this feedback and apologies for the confusion around our Downtown Store closure earlier this month. I'll pass along your feedback to our Purchasing team and am happy to answer any further questions via e-mail at info@citymarket.coop. Hope to see you back at the store soon!

name: adolfo alonso
text: Friendly and helpful staff! This is always my go-to grocery store or if i need some something really specific. Always have a great selection.

resp.text: Thanks for this kind feedback, Adolfo! We hope to see you in the store soon!

name: Jill E. Norman
text: I love City Market, because it's the only place that I can find Liberty's Yogurt. It's the best yogurt on earth !

resp.text: Thanks, Jill! We'll share this feedback with our Purchasing team and appreciate the love for Liberty's!

name: Alex Dombi
text: Offers a wide variety of local product for a good chunk of change. Definitely not a one-stop-shop in terms of grocery needs but rather where to go to find a defining flavor of a dish, bulk products in zero waste packaging, hot and ready cafe quality foods, or a daily coffee/tea/broth run. Kind staff but a damn slow checkout line, so budget that in.

name: ABL II
text: Dank foods.  I recommend the blue ledge richville cheese with persimmons on crackers.   The chicken livers are delish as well.

resp.text: Thanks for the feedback and product recommendations, ABL II! We will have to check that out.

name: Andrew Chase
text: If you are staying in the area for a short period of time, this place is perfect. It's very clean and ready to find what you need. Honestly, the food is better and faster than other local places if you just want to grab a breakfast sandwich and go!

name: TRP
text: Used to be better. I think this place has gone downhill over the years. I am glad there is Trader Joes nowadays because it is more affordable than city market. Customer service has gone down hill also and parking is pretty difficult sometimes. It's good if you're in a pinch or need something hard to get, but not for regular everyday purchases

name: Blossom Haven
text: The plantain chips I bought was expired... didn't know till I got home and was half way thru the snack... also an expensive place to shop

resp.text: Hi Blossom, so sorry to hear about your expired product. Could you e-mail us some more information at info@citymarket.coop so that we can issue you a refund and make sure we know what product you purchased? Thanks!

name: Thatcher Michelsen
text: Highest quality foods and vibes. Support your community shop local and thrive.

resp.text: Hi Thatcher, thanks so much for this kind review and our apologies for the late response! We appreciate your support and we're glad you're part of our community!

name: Peter
text:
So I'm not a vegan, or a crunchy hipster.  This is a fantastic market, you should probably bring your own bag(I popped in on vacation maybe Portland has a plastic bag ban?)
Bulk stuff, fresh actually human cut non vacuum pack meat, ugly health produce.
We were also able to pick up some pepperoni, name brand crackers and a fantastic selection of cheese.  stop in for a quick one or do a fancy meal planning.

name: Joseph Raczynski
text: Another fantastic market with a wide range of fresh produce and meats.

resp.text: Thanks for this kind feedback, Joseph! We're glad you were able to find what you were looking for!

name: ScapularBore
text: I love shopping here the service is good the only thing I do not like is the price on the products to high.

name: Mark Stein
text: This is one of my favorite places ever. Fun, funky staff, outstanding selection. It ain't cheap, but I find that the quality is usually very high. I tend to avoid the hot bar; I don't think it's a great value. The sandwiches, however, are fantastic. And the cozy eating area is one of my favorite wintertime people watching spots.

name: Ruth D.G.
text: Always find what I need & leave with a little extra. 🙂

resp.text: Hi Ruth, thanks for the feedback and review! Glad to hear you're able to find what you need and maybe even some items you didn't know you needed. Hope to see you again soon!

name: Rabbit 802 grow crew
text: Great people and produce!

name: Justin Bolio
text: I don't shop here but it's a very convenient location for my bank ATM

resp.text: Hi Justin, thanks for this feedback and glad you're able to use the Vermont Federal ATM! We'd love to have you shop with us in the store too, so if there's any feedback you want to share please e-mail us at info@citymarket.coop!

name: Ashraf Mohamed
text: Good products, but very expensive.

name: penny bolio
text: Over priced and snobs work there

name: Amy Sessock
text:
Excellent customer service!
I recently purchased a gluten free brownie mix and for whatever reason the directs provided did not life up to the delicious brownie experience I was hoping for. I inquired with customer service about my experience, since it was an expensive purchase (as gluten free products tend to be), without skipping a beat I was offered a refund. Feeling grateful for being a member of an establishment where loyalty, sympathy and customer service come first!

name: cynthia stephenson
text: Excellent quality food. Helpful friendly staff.

name: Matthew Jacobs
text: Little pricey but great staff and quality food.

name: Mg 0
text: Something about this truly natural, earth-friendly supermarket makes me want to buy everything in here. Loved that it has local produce—I bought and consumed an entire pint of Vermont blueberries from here recently.

name: Angie Pearson
text: Awesome place to shop

resp.text: Thanks Angie, hope you visit again soon!

name: engine rescue
text: Very friendly staff and good products

name: Ariel Jensen-Vargas
text: Our favorite!

name: Anabel Paz
text: City Market, It is not a place where you will find cheap prices, but the merchandise is very good even excellent quality ...

name: Brian Silver
text: VERY expensive. Crowded aisles difficult to maneuver. Not a terribly good selection of various products. Deli staff poorly trained, unfamiliar with their own products, unfamiliar with alternative products. Arrogant cashier. No thank you, and threw produce and delicate products into bag. Quality of produce quite good.

name: Andrew Polin
text: I would give another couple stars to the co op, however smoke free properties that promote the idea of smokers being less than automatically makes me want to visit this establishment less.  Dropping my review to 2 stars for the answer the Co Op gives.  They care about the comfort of non smokers and could not care less about the smokers.  I have no problem not smoking within 25 feet of an entrance.  But when you make me feel like a criminal for vaping as I get out of my car, I feel less than welcome.

resp.text: Hi Andrew - Thank you for that feedback. Our intent is enjoyment of the Co-op for everyone who stops by, not to make smokers feel less than. Because the Co-op is a gathering place for our community and many folks sit outside in various spots on the property, we want to make sure that the community feels comfortable lingering to visit with friends. We feel that offering a smoke-free property helps with that goal. If there's something we've done that makes you feel less than welcome here, please reach out directly and let me know. - Allison, ahope@citymarket.coop

name: JG DeBiasio
text: Best place for quality food, service and many local items.

name: Elisabeth ARTI Wulandari
text: Great Co-Op!! Bread! Vegies! Healthy snack!

name: Matias Gnass
text: July 2020 - bulk items in bins are not available for self serve; some are pre-packaged in small amounts. Deli is open and food is being served. 👍👍

name: Dann Doremus
text: Organic, vegetarian offerings. Nice Hot Bar for breakfast and Lunch. Great Bulk food dept with Teas and spices too

name: john wilcox
text: Great little grocery catering to whole and organic foods. My only real complaint is prices which are far too high on most of the organics. All considered though it's an inviting atmosphere with exceptional customer service.

name: Maddie O'Reilly
text: Great store with lots of local products and just about everything you'd be looking for. We found a local butter someone recommended to us (we're from out of town) and there were so many other delicious things. The store was clean and well organized/stocked.

name: Liisa Reimann
text: Well organized, huge variety, decent prices, awesome staff, best hot food bar around, and Miss Wienerz donuts (if you get there early enough). Why go anywhere else?

name: Marie Thomas
text: Awesome hot food bar.  Great place to grab a quick meal.  Lots of variety of foods.  Rally for change program  helps so many  non profits.  Some prices a little high, but all in a good cause.

name: Windsong young
text: The selection is healthier n locally sourced mostly the people and the atmosphere both r awesome

name: Nick Cart
text: Needs more vegan options!

resp.text: Hi Nick, thank you for sharing this feedback! We will pass this along to our Prepared Foods team. If you have other questions or suggestions, please feel free to e-mail us at info@citymarket.coop!

name: sean Jay
text: Amazing selection of local breads, veg, cheese, and more. There small sandwich station has some great stuff.

name: Sara C
text: Very nice organic grocery store. Lots of options, especially produce which looked so fresh & abundant. A little bakery & deli. Many healthy, vegan options, bulk spices, dried fruit, nuts, coffee, etc. It was expensive, but most of the health food type stores are.

name: Pattylynne Crichton
text: This is the best co-op in the country, and I've been to many. Great selection of local foods as well as national things. Great diverse staff as well. Oh, I love that they have an area to tie up dogs while shopping; we go almost everyday!

name: Kelsey Brandin
text:
It's great because of the convenient location and stock of city market's "greatest hits", but given its larger size and new construction, you'd imagine their inventory outshines the downtown store - it doesn't. Despite being closer to this location, i still drive into town for the better selection on both prepared food and groceries.
Good in a pinch or for simple stuff, but hopefully in the future they utilize the additional space appropriately and expand their inventory to match the smaller downtown location.

name: Kylie h
text: Love love love city market. Prices are what you would expect from a co-op. Many options. They make the best sandwiches ever. Everyone is friendly and knowledgeable. They have a great selection of many foods but to me my favorite is there selection of kombucha.

name: Renae Alexandria
text: City Market makes my life a better existence. Being a member is well worth it! We love the breakfast sandwiches they have available at the hot bar til 11am, and the free coffee after every 10 purchased is a nice perk :)

name: megan duffy
text: I have celiac disease so I always shop at Co-OP's. City Market is my local co-op. I love the store and the selection but the prices are a little high and the staff leave a LOT to be desired!

resp.text: Hi Megan, thanks for this feedback and so glad you're able to find some good gluten free options at the stores! I did want to make sure you knew about our Co-op Basics program. This is a line of everyday low price items and there are definitely some gluten free options there as well: https://www.citymarket.coop/basics! We'd also be happy to hear any additional feedback if you'd like to e-mail us at info@citymarket.coop. Thanks for the feedback and hope to see you in the store soon!

name: Sean Gauvreau
text: beautiful market with a great selection

name: Kara M.
text:
I liked this store a lot, it was like a less expensive and non-corporate version of Whole Foods.

This is a cute little market right near Church Street in Burlington, VT, it will only take a couple of minutes to walk over here.

We stopped in to get some hard ciders by a brand that we had sampled cider at earlier in the day at a local brewery.  They had a nice craft beer selection too.

They feature a lot of organic products and the produce looked nice.

I always enjoy a quick browse through this store while I'm in BTV.  I'd suggest coming here if you are staying nearby and looking for some snack items.

I'd describe this spot as a little on the granola side and very Vermont.

name: Elie Kaadi
text: Expensive but they have sushi Wednesdays lol

name: Andrew Swift
text: The local fresh food Co-op! There are other health food focused stores in the area, but City Market is the downtown favorite (with a second location coming in 2017).  Be prepared, the aisles are smallish. The fresh veggies and beer sections are exceptional. Also, great bakery items from all the local bakers. There is a deli section, fresh coffee and pastries and everything else you might need during a weekly grocery trip. In front, a generous table area, closed off from customer traffic. Also, outdoor seating in Summer (but limited). Prices are average, but getting a membership is worth it. Expect crowds during normal daytime breaks (lunch, after work). Excellent, friendly staff. Highly recommended!

resp.text: Hi Andrew - We're excited for the South End store as well (coming Fall 2017) which will have more aisle space and more parking! Thanks for sharing all your wonderful feedback; we'll be sure to share with staff who work hard to make your community-owned food co-op great!

name: L. A. Tisoncik
text: A great place to shop... Interesting foods, great bakery, great deli, and a bulk section I could spend too much time exploring.  The store is accessible but, as usual, some products are placed too high for wheelchair access (bulk, in particular, has a high counter in the spices and tea area for no good reason in my opinion) but both staff and customers are friendly and helpful with that impossibly high product location.

name: Richard K
text: Many quality high-end products, ethnic food, great produce, excellent deli, cheese selection, super sandwiches. Some items a bit pricey, but if you look for them you can some some good deals. Downtown store makes me claustrophobic, narrow isles, small store, always crowded. Prefer the new one on Flynn Ave. Worth joining the co-op if you shop there much for 10 % discount and yearly dividend.

name: Bluekimchi Andrea
text: I wish their space was laid out a little differently., as it gets crowded and aisles easily blocked. Prices are reasonable for organic, locally grown food. Some prices for things are a little high, yet no different than other natural foods stores in the area. Parking at peak times is crazy and they often have parking attendants to help out. I like their new space on Flynn Avenue very much

name: Irol Hunt
text: It's within walking distance. I have to be careful I usually go over my budget it's a little expensive.

name: Charlotte Reider-Smith
text: What a great place. They have everything and local stuff and stuff from all priceranges.

name: Josh Neilson
text: Great selection of organic produce and meats, as well as conventional products. Free filtered water for members, among other benefits. Deli, food bar, beer and wine. Seating for eating. Bulk herbs, grains, pastas... Parking can be nightmarish. Aisles are a little tight. Stilm my favorite place to shop for groceries in Burlington.

name: RoseMary Huebner
text: I love going here for lunch. They have the best hot buffet.

name: Pete Bruhn
text: Great selection, friendly people, delicious pre made foods & some of the best deli sandwiches around.

name: Molly Packard
text: Great place to get your organic foods. Little pricey but it's a nice store

name: Lucky Th13teen
text: Can't beat the bulk items quality to price. All our spices go further when we get them from here. Of course a little more expensive on the whole here but hard to fault it when you know where the $ ends up in comparison to any other grocery+ store.

name: G Aquino
text: It looks and feels like Whole Foods. Great selection of healthful and ethically sourced products, with prices that are a bit more reasonable than WF. Customer service was great. The only issue was the narrow aisles. Overall though, this place is pretty solid.

name: Caroline Frigon
text: Best place to find high-quality, organic, local goodies whenever you need them 😊 Customer service is also consistently good. Prices are high but fair.

name: Gavin Hieronymus
text:
Out of every grocery stores around the country and the world that I have gone to, this is the best one yet. The Onion River Co-op offers huge amounts of fresh, organic, and local produce, dairies, meats, spices, grains,  and almost everything else that you can think of. What they do not have from local farms, they make sure to buy the best goods they possibly can; just talking about it gives me that rare rush only a great grocery store can.

If you have the time and money for a good time and good meal, I beg that you go to the City Market in Burlington Vermont.

resp.text: Gavin - Thanks so much for your feedback! You certainly highlighted many of our favorite parts of the Co-op and many of the areas that set us apart from other stores. Glad we can give you a rush (we get the same thing when coming to work everyday)!!

name: Wylie Tharp
text: Great food, better people.

name: Stephen Furtado
text: Always like going here food is always good employee are friendly a little pricey but it's quality products

name: Liana Edwards
text: I love this grocery store. My favorite sections are the bulk items section and the hot buffet. There is always fresh produce and the staff are friendly.

name: William Eisner
text: Dazzling food selection emphasizes the healthy and local. Here  wine selection and cuisine intersect with politics and people watching. Makes one thankful for the rarified atmosphere that is VT.

name: Joshua O'Floinn
text: Great place for organic, local, and specialty foods. The physical space is pretty cramped. Often very busy and crowded during late afternoon & throughout evening. Often difficult to find parking. Early & mid mornings are the best time to visit if you want to avoid the crowd.

name: Joe Rivers
text: I don't know who's worse the people that shop there or the staff.

name: Mo Battah
text: Good place to buy groceries and sit in with coffee, pastry or cooked food

name: Matthew Hall
text: Great spot for a variety of healthy and unique choices.  A bit tight of a space but if that is bothersome, from an aisle or parking perspective, go visit their other store in Burlington.

name: Yoga Chick
text: The food on their Buffet always leaves me wishing it tasted a little bit different and the Big World while they sometimes have reasonable prices on conventional produce, for the most part a lot of their prices are just ridiculous

resp.text: Hi there - Thank you for the feedback; we compare our prices to other area retailers monthly, including the conventional big box grocers, and our prices are competitive. We indeed have "splurge-worthy" items on our shelves, but we also have every day low prices through our Co-op Basics program. In addition, we offer great sale prices every month through our combined Co-op purchasing power with other food co-ops across the country. And we offer our Food for All (FFA) program to community members who participate in 3SquaresVT, WIC or Social Security Disability or Supplemental Income. Our FFA program offers customers a 10% discount storewide and a 15% discount on Produce and Bulk, every time they shop (except alcohol, based on state law).

name: Mario Carmona
text: Good selection of organic foods. Hotbar is good most of the time. They have a nice made to order section for breakfast and lunch. Staff can be a bit crabby at times.  There’s a reason why there called City Markup, Get a loan or try hitting Trader Joe's for more reasonable prices

name: Ashley Lafleche
text: Excellent bulk selection. Friendly staff. Interesting and broad produce selection. Prices are reflective of a monopoly (because it is one). Also very crowded all the time due to the previous point.

name: Cole Phelps
text: Employees are pretty agro. Food is great though. Just wish I didn't get treated like trash at checkout

name: Bumble Bee
text: Honestly, I'm going to tell you straight up that everything's overpriced.  If you can get a store card or something it does help on some items.  It's often super packed, which can be a problem if you're just looking to grab something.    The staff are very worn out but seem to make an effort to be friendly.

resp.text: Hi Bumblebee Butts - I'm going to push back on your comment about everything being overpriced, although I do appreciate your four star rating! We sure do have splurge-worthy and specialty items, but we compare prices throughout the store against area competitors (including the corporately-owned grocery stores) every month. Our prices across the store are very competitive. Through our Co-op Basics program we offer 100s of "basic basket" products at very competitive every day low prices. Through our membership in a national group of food co-ops across the country, we get access to great sales on a wide array of products through our combined purchasing power and we pass these sales on to all customers. In addition, through our Food for All program, we offer a 10% storewide discount (with very few exceptions) and a 15% discount in Bulk and Produce to customers who participate in 3SquaresVT, WIC and Social Security Disability and Supplemental Income. Not sure what you meant by store card, but Co-op Members can volunteer with our Community Outreach Partners to be eligible for monthly store discounts (2 hours of volunteer work gets you a 7% discount and 4 hours of volunteer work gets you a 12% discount, for an entire month). If you'd like to discuss further, feel free to reach out directly! - Allison, ahope@citymarket.coop

name: Ryk Edelstein
text: Reliable supplier of all things organic.

name: Jamie Graham Gay
text:
There are two main things that have me shop here instead of the less expensive supermarkets in the area: consistently excellent produce section, and how they treat their employees and sellers. I really like that that they're unionized, and that they work so much with local farmers and food makers.

In addition to an excellent produce section, they also shine in ready-made food and bulk section.

The only downside is the small parking lot and rush hour shopping. Looking forward to the opening of their larger location in the South End.

resp.text: Thanks for the feedback, Jamie! We're looking forward to the South End Co-op as well (with more than 100 parking spaces in the plans....)! We partner with our local farmers and producers in so many ways (including a special flavor of butter with Ploughgate Creamery and Co-op Milk with Monument Farms) and also offer an amazing loan program to help them grow. While the parking lot at the downtown Co-op is small, there are bike parking spaces aplenty : )

name: Irene Waldock
text: They have everything a crunchy granola Vermonter could ever want! (Including a large section of bulk granola) With kombucha on tap and organic produce coming out the wazoo, it's the ideal grocery store if you can afford it.

name: Jim Woodard
text: I will start by saying their produce and meats are consistently fresh and high quality and I admit I enjoy shopping there.  The problem we had is with their system of special orders.  We ordered one item from both produce and meats for a special diner and only the meat arrived.  Since no one took our phone or email address they were not able to contact us.  This happened with an order we place three days in advance. Please update your systems to include a mode of communication to the customer.

resp.text:
Hi Jim,

Thanks for shopping with us and letting us know about this recent issue. We're taking a look at what happened on our side so that we can correct our mistake. The system we have in place for special orders typically requires that we take contact information precisely for this reason, so I'm not entirely sure what happened in this case. Regardless, I'm sorry that we didn't fulfill our promise to you. We'd like to make it up to you: could you send me an email at info@citymarket.coop with the date that you called and the produce items you ordered?

Yours in cooperation,
Todd

name: Sarah
text: Always helpful staff, great selections, great locations and good prices!

name: Starr Whitney
text: Its great. Hard to find what im looking for. But staff is always helpful

name: Nicole Crawford
text: Store was very clean and the staff was very helpful

name: Daniel Fortier
text:
CM/ORC has a manageable selection of good quality foods and general home products including a nice amount of locally sourced items. Relatively diverse customer base. A bit pricey but good deals can be had. They do participate in and support number of community hunger relief/food insecurity programs, as well as provide a number of discount programs, including "member worker" program that gives members discounts for volunteer work both in store, and several community partners. In store kitchen makes a cornucopia of delicious dishes that are sure to satisfy anyone, to conveniently eat there, or to take with.

Right now, they're selling Christmas trees for just $35 and in support of COTS, Committee On Temporary Shelter, who can always use our help, but especially this time of year!

resp.text: Well, Daniel, I couldn't have said it any better myself. You just offered up so many benefits to City Market membership and owning the store where you shop! Thanks for the feedback and we hope to see you again soon : )

name: Stephanie Black
text:
It's a good place to go if you want healthy, nutritious food but be ready to pay quite a bit for it! They're limited in what they have for generic brands. If you go there frequently it would be worth it to get their discount card. My only real complaint is the staff. Employees are not the friendliest and could use more training. I went in to shop about a month after giving birth to my daughter in 2015. I ended up in their bathroom hemorrhaging because of complications related to childbirth. No one else was with me at the time so I had to call an ambulance.
A couple of months later I went into city market again and after shopping I needed to use the restroom. On my way out of the store I was approached by an employee and asked to look up at their cameras (so they would have my photo). This employee proceeded to publicly humiliate me in front of dozens of other customers coming and going to the store. He told me they were having problems with people using drugs in their bathroom and wanted me to know that I was being watched because of when the ambulance had picked me up months prior. He assumed that I had overdosed in the bathroom. When I realized what he was saying I tried explaining to him the mix up, but he was not interested in hearing my side of the story. He told me that there were "places that could help people like me" and then he walked away while I was still talking.
I spoke with management afterwards and was given an apology but I'll never forget that horrible interaction. I was a loyal customer who shopped there nearly every day and now you're lucky to see me in there every six months. Horrible, horrible place.

name: Tatiana Gladkikh
text: A bit  pricey. Great variety of local, organic, vegan and vegetarian  food. For those who live in Burlington  area, I def recommend becoming the co-op member; members get a 12% discount on their purchase if they volunteer  at selected organizations for 4 hours a month.

name: Allan Bursaw
text: You can find any hard to get foods or drinks here without a doubt. It's a great local place and fun to get food at the sandwich shop. I love having a place like this in walking distance!

name: Ryk Edelstein
text: Clean, reliable and we'll stocked.

name: Barbara Oliver
text: I love the fresh vegetables, fruit & bulk items..but it's pricey.

name: Mac McGill
text: Nice market with local stuff. Hot bar is usually pretty great. Aisles are a bit narrow, especially as you first come in, and occasionally very crowded.

name: Scott Batdorf
text:
Best small grocery in the city!
Excellent hot bar and prepared foods..
Solid beer and wine selection.

name: Jay Furr
text: Despite it being at heart a "health food store", it has a little of everything.  The incredibly crowded parking lot and aisles are no mistake; it's super popular.  Great beer selection and great deli sandwiches and hot entrees.  Superior selection of produce.

resp.text: Jay - Thanks so much for your kind words! So glad you find what you need here and recognize that being busy means that we're keeping our Members and the greater community happy : ) We're looking forward to opening the South End store in late fall!!

name: Robert Bell
text: Why is healthier food so expensive?  Nice selection of healthier goods in a busy, crowded store. Hope you have good reflexes...you'll need them to dodge shopping carts in narrow aisles!

resp.text: Hi Robert - Thank you for your feedback and the 4 star rating : ) We are indeed a bustling, community-owned food co-op and we fit a lot of choices into a fairly small space. Your note about healthier food being expensive is a topic of much conversation, especially for locally-owned food co-ops. We have combined buying power through our National Co-op Grocers' purchasing contracts, which helps keep our prices on many products competitive. And while we offer plenty of "splurge-worthy" items, we also have everyday low prices on a number of products in every category through our Co-op Basics program. We compare prices with area retailers every month to ensure that our prices are competitive. If you have feedback about a specific product price, I'd be happy to discuss further in person. - Allison Hope, Director of Community Engagement, ahope@citymarket.coop

name: Madeline Ostlund
text: Expensive but you ggt what you pay for

name: Althea Greene
text: City market is a great local co-op. It's in downtown Burlington so it's walkable and it offers a wide variety of local and natural foods and specialty products like vegan ice cream and seitan. The parking lot can be crazy so I recommend walking if possible and the aisles are narrow and tend to be crowded so get a basket rather than a cart.

name: stefan otto
text:
Great selection of local organic fruits, veggies and meat. Good beer selection as well. Fantastic bulk foods section with big selection. Local bread and cheese.
Beware of tight squeeze in parking lot!

name: Deborah Blair
text: Love this co-op! It is huge -it offers both regular grocery store items and a huge variety of locally produced products and health food products. There is a parking lot  - which in the center of Burlington is a real plus! Although I now live across the state - we always have a list going for what we need from City Market. They have a huge variety of organic and non organic vegetables and fruits - their large hot and cold bars are great for getting a lunch, snack or taking home food to add to ones home cooked meals. I always find the staff to be friendly and helpful - - and the help desk has hand outs to help find the Gluten Free and other specialty health diet needs for those needing them for medical and personal choice needs. They have a great variety of beers, wines, bulk food nuts, flours, etc - - Kombuchas AND they have Vermont Kombucha in many flavors that you can buy or bring your own containers to fill up  - they also have grass fed Vermont meats, sea food  - - really anything that you could want!

name: Silvia F
text: The reverse osmosis water is free for members. There is a tremendous amount of local and organic produce, and products, and enviroment-friendly items. The hot and salad bar is always topped off and tidy. There are several different hot coffees to choose from. The coffee lid dispenser is clever. The sandwich station is popular for great reasons. The cheese selection is delightfully overwhelming. The cashiers are friendly and fast. The bicycle parking is spacious. When the car lot is full there is a parking coordinator that helps the flow to go smoother.

resp.text: Silvia - Thanks so much for sharing your positive feedback online! Your use of adjectives is stellar; maybe we'll have to have you write some ad copy for us in the future! Phrases like "delightfully overwhelming" make our hearts sing here at the Co-op : )

name: Neil Marriott
text: City Market is a great place all the way around....great grocery store with good food, good staff, good vibe with a great moral code. There should be more companies like City Market much less grocery stores..

name: Nicholas Glass
text: The bulk foods are amazing! beer and wine section is as good as you can get without going to a store for it in Vermont (which in Vermont means you have one of the best beer grocery store selections in the country; Vermont knows beer). Amazing vibe. Your getting higher quality then the chains around here and you taste the quality, and at the risk of sounding "new age", you can feel the quality when you eat it.

name: Douglas Levine
text: Parking is horrible at this location, you have people walking right behind you when your backing out, and you have cars driving behind you when backing out.

name: George Mihaly
text: This COOP does it right! Awesome selection of local produce from farmers just a few miles away. Staff if super friendly/outgoing and eager to chat with you. Being a City Market member also gives you some great discounts with local businesses. This is the place to shop for food stuff in Burlington!

name: Clifford Gordon
text: Great selection of locally sourced products and organic foods. Very busy place and would benefit from wider isles and more floor space. Love the meads they stock here. Can't find them anywhere else.

name: MP Hedges
text: Well, it's not a chain and the access by foot, bike or car (horrors!) is sufficient. Not everything passes tree hugger militant standards, but for the most part you can make Earth-friendly buying choices.

resp.text: Hi MP - indeed we are a hybrid community-owned Co-op and one of a handful that we know of around the country. When we became the downtown grocery store in 2002 and were leasing the land from the City of Burlington, we signed an agreement to change up our model a bit and ensure that we were accessible to the entire community. So we don't have a buying policy like many other Co-ops do and we leave space for customers and Members to make choices that work for their specific needs and families and diets and such. Thanks for visiting and we hope to see you again soon! - Allison, ahope@citymarket.coop

name: Rebecca Myer
text: Great place for most organic items you may be looking for. Local variety is great. Some items are pricey, bulk section is amazing!!

name: Jaimie Bernstein
text: Great bagel sandwiches and wonderful vegan options!

name: Cat Apeiron
text: They're pretty fast and efficient here. Nice place.

name: Oliver Ames
text: Fresh and local, this is the place to go for organic produce. They also have a great buffet which is popular amongst the college crowd. I've had a few terrible experiences trying to get Apple Pay to work on their Apple Pay registers (not checkout's fault but management). This place is worth it for the food. They're very helpful and accommodating with special orders too which is a major win in my book.

resp.text: Thanks for the feedback, Oliver! Glad you enjoy the produce and the housemade food on our buffet. I apologize that we're not meeting your needs with Apple Pay. Technically, our current point of sale system won't support Apple Pay or Google Wallet (it should be part of the next version we receive later in the summer/early fall). That said, you can try it on many lanes, but if it doesn't work, our software manufacturer doesn't offer any support for us to fix it at this point. If you have more questions on that, feel free to be in touch directly with Allison at allisonw@citymarket.coop. See you soon!

name: Jane Day
text: City Market is a great community store

name: Kavi Raj Joshi
text: Relatively expensive. However, liked the way they appreciate and promote local products.

name: Randy Pulsifer
text: Lots of items and food. High towering shelves. Crowded and easy to get lost.

resp.text: Hi Randy - Thank you for leaving a review! We do offer a lot of choices in a small footprint, so we try to maximize space as much as possible. Our shelves aren't too much different than conventional grocery stores, but the Co-op's aisle are a little narrower which leads to often being in close proximity to other shoppers : ) We hope it makes for a cozy shopping environment where you see lots of your friends (or make new ones)! - Allison, ahope@citymarket.coop

name: Michael Robinette
text: Now that there are 2 stores you can always find parking. The store has a great selection of everything and they sell great prepared food.

name: Justin Anderson
text:
Love this store. Food is so fresh and healthy.
Slightly costly.

resp.text: Hi Justin - Thank you for the feedback! We work hard to make sure that our prices are competitive, so I'd love to hear more about any specific items that you felt were too expensive. Each month, we price compare items throughout the store with natural and conventional grocers in our area to make sure our prices are competitive. In addition, we offer a Food for All (FFA) Program for customers who participate in 3SquaresVT, WIC or Social Security Disability or Supplemental Income. Our FFA Program offers 10% off storewide each time participating customers shop and 15% off our Produce and Bulk departments. We also have a Co-op Basics program with hundreds of items set at everyday low prices, many which are lower than our area competitors. Of course, we do have many splurge-worthy products as well in a number of different categories, for those days when you want to treat yourself : ) - Sincerely, Allison Hope, Director of Community Engagement, ahope@citymarket.coop

name: Mary Liesenberg
text: SO OVERPRICED, but some unique items that are worth the trip! Couldn’t do the regular groceries here but occasionally come for treats. If you wanna be healthy at a better price try Healthy Living.

resp.text: Hi Mary - I'm curious which products you are finding overpriced at the Co-op. While we certainly have many specialty and "splurge-worthy" products, we also have hundreds of products that we offer at very competitive every day low prices through our Co-op Basics program. In addition, our Food For All program offers customers who use WIC, 3SquaresVT or Social Security Disability or Supplemental Income a 10-15% discount on groceries each and every day. Our Members who volunteer with one of our 22 Community Outreach Partners can also earn 7% or 12% discounts for volunteering 2 to 4 hours per month. Stop by on Thursdays to receive 10% off purchases from our Bulk Department or stop in Tuesday to receive 10% off supplements. We compare our pricing with area competitors regularly and are often lower than the conventional grocers. If you have specific suggestions for improvement, I'd be happy to listen. - Allison Hope, Director of Community Engagement, ahope@citymarket.coop

name: Craig Bushey
text: Good food a great healthy selection but it is way overpriced don't go here if your on a budget

resp.text: Hi Craig - Thanks for the feedback! We have a number of different programs to ensure that we are very competitively priced. Our everyday low price program, Co-op Basics, allows us to offer hundreds of items in a variety of categories at great prices. We offer a Food for All (FFA) program for customers on 3SquaresVT, WIC or Social Security Disability/Supplemental Income. This innovative program offers a 10% grocery discount for FFA Members each time they shop - saving these customers collectively over $200,000 last year alone. We also compare our prices to area competitors, including the larger conventional grocers, each month. From this data, we know that are prices are very competitive for our area. We certainly have some splurge-worthy items across the store, but we've got something for every budget as well! If you have feedback about a specific product or price point, I'd love to hear from you directly. - Sincerely, Allison (ahope@citymarket.coop)

name: Jay I
text: Wow...wish we had one in manchester vt..

name: C RC
text: Very good variety...close to downtown.

name: Joe Beaird
text: Excellent selection of local, Vermont foods. Also good for a quick bite or coffee.

name: Jeffrey R
text: Check out the soups they change daily and are priced accordingly.  Great place to find healthy foods.   The eating area is small and ALWAYS full,  Just a suggestion . . . maybe reduce the parking lot size and make the eating area larger. <--- just an idea . .

name: Michael Johnson
text: Local market. Limited brand and products. Urban priced. But convenient to right downtown.

name: Marna Ehrech
text: One of my favorite food stores... And the deli makes great GF breakfast sandwiches! Call ahead and it will be ready for pickup when you get there!

name: mike Mr. Bear
text: I've worked here for nearly 13yrs because I love the people I work with, the customers I cater to,   and the camaraderie.

name: Megan Niquette
text: Found my new favorite bulk tea here. Great place with unique and tasty items!

name: Zewo Maluk
text: I love city market/onion River coach _

name: Haley Colburn
text: The sandwiches here are absolutely amazing. They're very generous with their portions and bread, meat and veggies are always fresh!

name: Ben Carpenter
text: Very nice/healthy food with a great selection and service with a hot bar and is very convenient as it I'd right in downtown Burlington. Great place to shop for all your grocery's!

name: Nathon Horton
text: Awesome co-op. An employee saw me and my 3 year old looking at some produce and gave him a small toy. Made his day and reflected their overall friendliness.

name: Peg Purdue
text: Awesome market and a great place to grab a healthy lunch. Very helpful staff for the most part.

name: Jason Kanellis
text: The hot maple ginger bone broth at the food court is out of this world.

name: Keely Sir-Potato
text: The sandwich counter has delicious options. The line is always long and for good reason!

name: Heather Tackett
text: At times the market can be very busy and parking horrible. But if you go early morning to mid afternoon it is not so bad. They have an amazing bulk section of beans,  spices, granola, and baking powders making it easy to getting small portions of things you don't use every day but need for a new recipe. They also have tons of local products and organic items. Thier seafood counter maybe small but I have never had a problem with the quality of thier fish. I really enjoy shopping here and will definitely continue to!

name: Sherry Dupee
text: Great place. Good selections of groceries. Can buy small or large quantities of some things

name: Ronni
text: Always busy. Clean. Expensive. Staff can be helpful.

name: Jacob Goo
text: Great variety of organic foods and healthy choices, they make great cold brew too!

name: Oliver Scanlon
text: Always have very good food.  The store is not huge and is a little crowded at busy times but it's a nice place.  Beware that parking is a hassle as it's almost always packed.

name: Nicolas Bussière
text: Love this place with a lot of great food products and excellent service. I always find everything there.

name: Gregory Wilkins
text: Pricey, but they do have good and healthy options if you're looking for something quick to eat. They also stock a lot of unique beers, mead and ciders in their cooler.

name: Jack Evans
text: Good prices for a lot of fresh local produce. Has affordable conventional options when needed. Food bar has great food, and the staff is helpful.

name: Christie Jerry
text: I dont like how small it is inside. There is no room to have a cart unless u want to bump into everything in the isle or ppl. Customer service is moderate depending on what u look like. I feel as though you have to be a hippie and where petrulie to get good customer service and the prices r ridiculous.

resp.text: Hi Christie - I'm sorry that you didn't have a good experience at the Co-op! We are indeed limited in space, but still try to offer everything our customers might need to do all of their grocery shopping here. If you want more elbow room, our South End store on Flynn Avenue is the place for you! Our customers are a very diverse group and we aim to offer them all the best customer service possible; if you have specific areas where we could do a better job, please feel free to be in touch. In terms of prices, we have an every day low price program that offers hundreds of products at great prices. We price compare with all of our area competitors each month to ensure that we're priced appropriately - we are lower than some of the area's conventional grocers and right in line with others. We also offer our popular Food For All Program for customers who use 3SquaresVT, WIC or Social Security Disability or Supplemental Income. This Program offers our FFA Members 10% off their groceries each time they shop and 15% off purchases from the Bulk and Produce departments. So there are lots of ways to save at the Co-op! - Sincerely, Allison (ahope@citymarket.coop)

name: Ethan Farmer
text:
City market has an amazing selection of fresh, local produce and products. The staff are exceptionally helpful and friendly and the hot bar/sandwiches are delicious.

Joining the co-op and volunteering gets you a discount as well, and gives you an opportunity to get out in the community.

resp.text: Hi Ethan - Thanks for your feedback; you really mentioned many high points of owning a share of the Co-op! We'll share your kudos with our Prepared Foods team who makes the great food for our hot & cold food bar and deli sandwiches every day. If you're a Member, now's the time to also think about running for the Board (find more info at http://www.citymarket.coop/elections-2016).

name: Kimberly Cummins
text: This coop has a little bit of everything for everyone.  Great prepared foods department and stocked shelves with both organic, natural and conventional products.  Lots of local organic produce and an excellent bulk deparment.

resp.text: Thank you for the rating and the feedback, Kimberly! We just made some delightful improvements to our bulk department; feel free to let us know what you think : )

name: Mitchell Wulfman
text: I shopped here almost every day for a year, before I moved.  Great products and good customer service.  It gets super crowded during shopping hours though, and it's expensive (it's lovingly nicknamed "City Markup").  Also the parking lot is literally a road, so there's often nowhere to park.

name: omniscient
text: Always fresh and great sandwich shop. Great for vegan/veterinarian and health concience shoppers.

name: Sir Joshua Choiniere
text: The only place I shop! Organic non GMO and not as processed if at all. Free reverse osmosis water as a member and tastes better than spring water. Get a check in November as a member as well. Tons of college ladies.  Nuff said

name: Jessica Church
text: Too expensive too crowded rude cashier deli didn't have products that would have liked no smiles from anyone no greatings no friendly service overall I think it sucked

name: Carmen George Weddings
text: Wonderful selection of Vermont cheeses, maple syrup and coffee. Staff is the cheese department know what they are talking about. Go early, bike or walk to avoid the insane parking lot.

resp.text: Hi, A - Thank you for your kind words! Our cheese case is certainly a thing of beauty and we try to ensure our staff is well trained about our products and our Co-op and always with an eye toward great customer service. I'm glad that you had a good experience and we hope to see you again soon!

name: Jme Cole
text: Great market. Great staff. Something's are overpriced.

name: Adam Dyer
text: Love this place. Great place for local produce. Staff can be a little judgy at times but what can you do? It is Burlington.

name: ENS SI
text: Their parking situation is a disaster.  Too crowded with entitled college students, and too expensive.  Their employees are hit or miss I've found, either very helpful or snotty.  And YES, I said I want plastic, not paper.

name: Douglas Hood
text: This place has a nice array of local and local-ish ingredients. There's a nice hot bar, as well. It is usually really crowded, though.

name: Andre C.
text: Fantastic local produce, great beer selection, convenient eat-in options.  The staff are great, too.  Only complaint is that the parking lot gets quite chaotic and the store is often crowded, it's difficult to navigate with a stroller.

name: Sam Urbôn
text: The hot bar is great and reasonable, service is good, but it's crowded. Produce /meat/fish prices are DOUBLE, sometimes triple of what other stores charge. Extremely expensive except for dry goods and hot bar.

resp.text: Hi, Sam - Thanks for sharing your feedback! The hot/cold food bar is indeed busy, especially at lunch and dinner times! Because much of our meat selection is local and/or organic, you will find that it is more expensive than the commodity meat that you find at other retailers. Our Produce Department offers both conventional and organic options and we do compare our prices (in this department and across the store) to other retailers in the area each month to ensure we're competitive. If there are specific items you'd like to talk about, feel free to email me at aweinhagen@citymarket.coop. Thanks!

name: Chris Bergen
text: This is a great store with options for all dietary preferences, especially for health conscious folks or those with allergies (gluten, dairy, corn, etc). Their hot bar buffet is GREAT. Expect horrendous parking congestion and in-store claustrophobia. This is a tiny store for all the business it does.

name: Ildiko P
text: Love,love love this place...Great selection of fresh local produce and more. Delicious buffet style fresh food with so much to choose from.

name: Dan Hall
text: Great location, good produce and great bulk section. Seafood leaves something to be desired--better at healthy living. Customer service is sometimes rude.

name: Steve Kaplowitz
text: It is the "ONLY" place I have ever shopped where I know that the "GREATER" majority of my money is used to support this community here in Burlington.

name: Jesse Gaboriau
text: A wonderful grocery store chock full of fine foods from a farm down the road to a coast off Asia. There deli and hot food bar is great if you're in a hurry and church street is too busy.

name: Justin C
text: Love this place. It's my go to spot to get quick food and beer when I'm in Burlington!

resp.text: Hi, Justin - Many thanks for giving us "go to" status!! Our Prepared Foods team does a great job making wonderful food for our hot and cold food bar, our grab and go case and our sandwich station. And our local beer scene, well, it keeps us and our customers quite happy : )

name: Sam Stelfox
text: Good healthy and primarily local grocery store. Member owned with additional benefits to being a member. The sandwich & food bar are surprisingly tasty as well for quick eats.

name: Killian Hermann
text: Downtown monopoly on groceries and it shows. Cramped and dirty. Consistently terrible buffet. Always long register lines that block shoppers. Poor selection with a bizarre and inconsistent ethical bent. One extra star because when there isn't a 10 minute wait to order a sandwich those are pretty good, but really this place just f'ing sucks out loud but they have an entire town held hostage and apparently are accountable to nobody in any meaningful way.

resp.text: Hi Killian - I'm sorry that you haven't had great experiences at the Co-op. We aim to meet the entire community's needs through a diverse product selection, with a focus on local and made in VT products. Our hot and cold food bar is popular, so if you have specific feedback about dishes you didn't like, I'd love to hear it so we can continue to improve. The City initially leased the Co-op the land to build the Downtown store and we continue to be accountable to City Councilors and officials, our Members and the greater community. You can find our Annual Report on our website at www.citymarket.coop/annualreport to read about ways that we support and meet the needs of the Burlington-area community. (Allison Weinhagen, Director of Community Engagement, aweinhagen@citymarket.coop)

name: Rachel Wassel
text: Great co-op, supports your local community , huge amount of organic and natural products. Also great bulk section!

name: Sean
text: I love city market besides one thing... the parking!!!! Ahhh I want to tear my hair out every time I visit this place. People driving seem to be more inconsiderate then anywhere else besides Costco lol. Other than that great products and an awesome variety of unique and quality items.

name: Eric Potter
text: A great co-op City Market. Lots of good food choices for everyone. Prices are pretty good even if you are not a member.

resp.text: Thanks for your great feedback, Eric! The prices you see at the shelf are the same for Members and non-Members so we can be a welcoming environment for everyone. Members get many benefits, including participating in our Patronage Refund program where we return a portion of our profits from Member sales back to our Members each year. We also just started our new Co-op Basics program which offers great prices on a wide range of products throughout the store!

name: Derp Derpington
text: If I wear a backpack into a business first thing I do is ask staff if they have a backpack policy and it's ok. Went in and looked for staff and as soon as I walked in an older female employee glared at me and started harassing me and telling me to leave immediately. I explained I was going to ask if it was ok but she just insisted on being a b*tch for no reason. Fire that POS and maybe you'll regain my business.

resp.text: Hi there - I'm sorry this was your experience at the Co-op! I'd appreciate you sending more information directly to me so I can better understand what happened and discuss with the folks involved. City Market doesn't have a backpack policy, we just ask that customers shop into a basket or cart rather than into their bag or backpack. And unless we've trespassed someone or there are other mitigating circumstances, we aren't ever in the habit of asking anyone to leave. We are a community-owned store that is welcoming to all! - Allison Hope (ahope@citymarket.coop)

name: Brennan Martin
text: Handy place for groceries downtown.  Decent selection given small footprint.  Parking lot can be challenging.

name: Kiki Kirkland
text: Love their sandwiches and there is a make your own salad bar should go there.

name: Jasmine DeLude
text: I like the location, and that I can buy local, however I wish there was more variety, including conventional, I also wish there was more space to move around it's always packed. Price is pretty high, but local food costs more everywhere.

resp.text: Hi Jasmine - Thanks for taking the time to rate the Co-op and offer some feedback! With limited shelf space, we're continuously reviewing our offerings to make sure that we offer enough variety for customers (mostly based on how things are selling and what the regional/national trends are). With the variety comes products for each budget, whether it's bacon, toothpaste, produce or cereal. There's the potential for more elbow room in the store once we open our second location in the South End of Burlington next fall (we assume about 20% of our downtown business will head that way) : )

name: kyle brown
text: It's a great store the prices are a little high being my only complaint.

name: Elliot Schwartz
text: Good mix of conventional and organic products, with local offerings well labeled. Extensive bulk section. Late hours are handy.

name: Corey Gilmore
text: Prices are very high and it is constantly filled with yuppies and granola heads.  Lots of local offerings.  Lots of premade foods and sandwiches which are usually very good.  Still, if you like your money and don't want to deal with being judged not showing up on a bicycle, there are better places for shopping.

resp.text: Hi Corey - We're always happy to talk more about pricing and customer service and appreciate specific feedback so we can improve; if you're interested, please feel free to email us directly at info@citymarket.coop. We do conduct pricing surveys of all area stores every month and our prices compare favorably. In each product category, we do our best to offer options that meet any budget's price points, so our customers are free to choose options that meet with their values, their budgets and any other filters they use to shop for food.

name: Quinn Reid
text: Natural and bulk foods, local organic produce, plus more conventional goods. Hot foods bar, sandwich counter, good beer and wine selection.

name: Nicole Draper
text: Great selection. Love the bulk foods. Some thing are pricey.

name: Gabriel Harwood
text: Great organic selection and bulk foods with a bit of variety thrown in. Their prepared foods are great and beer selection is top notch. It is a bit pricey for daily shopping, but worth it for the convenience.

resp.text: Hi, Gabriel - Thanks for the feedback! On pricing, we aim to have products at a variety of price points in each category - budget stretchers, everyday low prices through our Co-op Basics program, and "splurge-worthy" items. If you notice specific prices that seem out of line, please drop us a note so we can review. We compare our prices with all of our area competitors each month to ensure we understand and react to the competitive landscape.

name: Cheryl Niedzwiecki
text: Being in culinary education, tho is one of my favorite places to go. I love it!!!

name: Mike Grill
text: Great selection, high prices. I enjoy eating food from here, but please, make it cheaper!!

name: Anne Hall
text: Love City Market , not so much the parking . Great selection for produce , bulk foods and spices. Love to have lunch there as well !

name: Emily Reynolds
text: Pay staff great, good food, kind pricey.

name: Mike Boltz-Robinson
text: Great when it comes to fruit and vegetables.  Also great beer and wine selection.

name: Brian Caruso
text: Great selection of staple items, prepared foods, craft beer & desserts. But it's always packed with people, so be prepared.

name: Ann Ely
text: I like this store , especially for organic, humanly raised chicken.  Great vegetables, and fruits.  My two biggest complaints: parking can be difficult on certain days and different times of the day.  Also, the isles in the market are small and shoppers can be rather rude by pushing past others. Also, the fruit/veggie spot is rather congested.

name: lilsmomma1
text: Great selection of quality, organic products, spices, hard-to-find items, health and beauty products.  Friendly staff, community-minded.

name: Brooke L-J
text: Great produce and bulk food section! The sandwiches and hot food bar are great too.

name: Ben Soltsov
text: Good place for lunch or to pick up some cold brews

name: Charles Lambert
text: A good place to get fresh subs !!

name: Mikhael Cohen
text:
Best co-op, period. Best local foods store. Highest grossing single-location co-op in the nation. When I moved back from a year in Hawaii, this is one of the things I looked forward to most. I've lived in a few places, and no other store compares.

Gluten-free? Vegan? Conventional diet? They have everything.

What's good:

Produce. Local and distant, organic and conventional. Pricing is fair.

I don't wish to promote meat or animal products, but they have the best local selection of this stuff, if you're going to buy, don't buy from the conglomerates.

BULK. Bulk everything, in exactly the amount you need. Teas, coffee, pasta, soup, baking needs, grains, nuts, snacks, candy, dried fruit, peanut butter, Dr. Bronner's, dish soap, laundry detergent, olive oil, maple syrup, the list goes on. Bring your own container or use theirs. Tare your own bottle on the scale right nearby.

Hot bar. Cheapest in town, always good food. Selection doesn't change as frequently as I'd like, but it's always good. It does bother me quite a bit when I see staff grab the spoon that landed in the chicken and put it back in a vegan dish, but at least they offer a good vegan selection.

Great bread from most local bakeries. Cookies, chocolate, beer and wine selections are all grand.

Deli is great. Grab a bagel in the morning, they'll prepare it however, they have everything for it. Grab a coffee. Sit and use the Wi-Fi in the eating area. It's somehow magically distant enough from the commotion to be semi-peaceful.

Oh, there is that. Remember how this is the highest grossing single location co-op in the nation? It's busy. All the time. Have patience for your neighbors, we're all in this together. And hey, they're expanding to Pine St soon!

To add to this point, the parking lot can be hell during commuting times. I'm surprised more people/cars aren't hurt here. It's too small, and people are too hurried.

The staff are all great, I feel like I'm in there so much they're always part of my life. Extremely helpful if help is ever needed. It's well-managed, and they take great care of their staff. They're involved in about 17 community volunteering efforts and ever-expanding, with very significant discounts to members who volunteer in their community.

Open til' 11 EVERY night, after my day is beyond over I can still go in and grab some food.

Great place, can't recommend highly enough. Could be my most favorite business in town. In fact it is.

We hope that you'll attend one of our community engagement sessions to review plans for the South End store; we'll be holding them in Spring 2016 and will share dates/times/locations early in the year. See you soon!

resp.text: Hi Steven - Indeed our Downtown store is bustling and busy; that's the environment many of our Members and customers like. But if not, perhaps our South End store is more your speed? It has the same great products, but also has more elbow room for customers and for staff (part of the reason we built a second store was to alleviate some of the pressure on the Downtown store). On the pricing front, I'm curious if you have specific items that give you the impression we're overpriced. We price compare with area grocers, conventional and natural, every month to make sure we're very competitive. Our Co-op Basics program offers hundreds of every day items (many organic too) at great prices - some even less than the conventional grocers. And our Food for All program offers customers who participate in 3SquaresVT, WIC or Social Security Disability or Supplemental Income a 10% discount on groceries storewide and a 15% discount on our Produce and Bulk Departments. Members can also get a discount at either store for volunteering with our over 22 Community Outreach Partners. We make sure that we offer fair prices, as well as plenty of other ways to save. So while we definitely offer many "splurge-worthy" products, we also have great prices in every category throughout both stores. name: Nate Merrill
text:
Tire Warehouse is what you would expect of a store that sells and installs tires. The selection fulfills most tire needs; I however had my online tire purchased shipped here for free and paid TW to install them.
The staff was efficient, very helpful and friendly. The installation process was quick and effortless on my part. The hours are great; it was easy just driving in and having the work done.
The general physical demeanor, as stated previously, is typical: functional, not attractive. Tires strewn across the showroom floor, basic chairs for waiting and dust covering pretty much everything. But, for the short time spent waiting, it was not unpleasant. And the free wifi is fast enough for videos. Bonus: the bathroom was clean.
4.5 stars.

Extremely rude staff.  Drive through could not get our order correct.  When we refused it, we were told to "leave and never come back".  Upset at their attutude, my daughter and I went inside to talk to a manager.
Offending associate refused to give me his name and threatened to call the police on me because I wanted to complain.
Horrible, horrible, horrible!
Will never return.
