name: Brandon Watson
text: I don’t even know where to start. From the front door to the exit this place is amazing. The service, the hostess, the food, the appetizers, the atmosphere, absolutely everything is exceptional. Would recommend this to everyone and I would come back over and over

name: Everett Ackerman
text: A scrumptious lunch with excellent service. The onion soup was dynamite at warming you up from the cold outside. Crispy fries alongside the chicken sandwich was delightful while the hot beef melt was sweet, salty and all goodness. Amazing experience as always at Leunigs.

name: GRACE MCINTOSH
text:
One of our favorite place to go. The atmosphere is great and the service is always good.
We had escargot, foie gras, and steak frites.

name: Craig Knowles
text: Food was absolutely delicious from the soup, pasta, French dip and chicken sandwich....the drinks were on point and dessert was awesome the maple creme Brule was awesome.

name: Kimberly McGowan
text: This place is amazing! We had the Vermont trio sliders, duck fat kettle chips, duck tacos, beef, and maple creme brûlée. It’s a little on the expensive side, but definitely a good value for the price. We would definitely come back again!

name: William D
text: Got the Pumpkin Alfredo and my SO got the Filet Mignon. Our food was incredible, service was friendly, and the entire city of Burlington was amazing. I'd love to return sometime.

name: Todd Tomasi
text: On point. COVID-19 seating accommodations were excellent. You actually feel like you have the place all to yourself at times.  Went for lunch and they are now serving their special Bistro menu from noon on. Drinks were super good... Service was just right.  Hanger steak was delicious, tried the new oysters Po Boy sandwich. Concept itself was good but to be 100% honnest the fried oysters were a little bit fishy and possibly not super fresh. I totally get it with stocking/ordering shellfish during the covid slow down can be tricky. Remulade was interesting, sweet and almost fermented but I personally think a homemade mayonnaise ailo or fresh dill tartar sauce would be better.  Just my foodie two cents here. Overall a great experience.

name: Torsten Bergersen
text: It’s okay. Large portions but lacking in flavor and quality. Good for a casual meal

name: Mahraz Amini
text:
very nice place, very clean , polite servants, good service. the price of the food are high! and the portion of the food is small. I order fillet for the lunch at it came with small amount of arugula and it was really small fillet(8oz probably) for 22$. it was really delicious but I was hungry right after eating my fillet. known as the second best restaurant in Burlington's down town.

Also went there for brunch. the steak and egg fries and cheese was good, delicious and still seems a little bit over priced to me.

name: Zachary Hubbell
text: Good for lunch  and dinner! Fantastic wine selection, outdoor seating and live music!

name: Neil Boylan
text: My go-to dining experience in Burlington, VT. Whether it’s for brunch, lunch, dinner, or just meeting for drinks, Leunig’s is your spot. Everything is good. It truly is a combination of Vermont + France. Enjoy!

name: Christopher Lei
text: The beef bourguignon pictured here. Great deal as part of the $20 menu.

name: Mike Gibbons
text: Great experience, great good, socially distant

name: Kelsey Mattoon
text: Excellent Vermont coffee. Have gone for brunch and dinner. Can't go wrong! The creamy mashed with the beef bourguignon was divine! Very tender, rich and great balance of flavors. Only complaint is I wish there was more mashed potatoes and carrots. Brunch has nice variety that changes with the seasons. Great place to sit outside too

name: Glenn Harshman
text: good food outside seating

name: Ryan Peacock
text:
I honestly can't say anything bad about this place. The decor is nice and the foods pretty good.

I don't think I'd go back, during my stay in Burlington (Maybe during the summer to see what it looks like opened up) but it's worth visiting.

The truffle fries were really good! Can't speak to the quality of the foie gras, as I've never had it before, and it's entirely possible I just don't like foie gras.

Worth a try though.

name: Casey McClain
text: Excellent food and service at a great location. A five star experience with 3.5 star pricing. Food is excellent and worth well above the price it is served at. The atmosphere is attempting a French Bistro style and does a fair job for downtown Burlington. The drink selection is excellent, a bit on the pricey side but still not far above average. This is a restaraunt I can't help but recommend to anyone looking for an excellent gourmet level meal with a good atmosphere in the Burlington area.

name: Kenneth J
text: Excellent service and a delicious dinner meal! Highly recommend a visit here! The stuffed chicken is great!

name: Ted Grzesik
text: Best food in Burlington. You will not be disappointed

name: Tracey Morrow
text: Fabulous, as always. I have never had a bad meal here, and I don't recall being disappointed at all ever. The service today was a bit slow, but only because it's December 14 and they were very busy. The food arrived hot and fresh, so it is not because it was sitting. We shared escargot to start and it was delicious. Butter, herbs, garlic, a little cheese, toasted bread...I could eat that all day! The herbs and garlic added to the flavor without overwhelming the delicate escargot, which were tender. I then had the quinoa crusted shrimp on naan. Perfection. The bread was soft and moist, the shrimp crunchy and perfectly cooked. The garnishes added to--again--without overpowering the shrimp. Service was excellent.

name: Katrina Vince
text: Service was wonderful. Stu at the bar and Ron at the table was great.  Simple meal: eggs and sausage.  Scrambled eggs with grease yum.  Sausage links were more dehydrated.  Even had others try... nope not sausage.  Perhaps just an off day in the kitchen.

name: Christopher Poudrette
text: Had lunch here with my girlfriend and we thought it was amazing. The food and wine were great and it had a nice atmosphere. We were here during Mardi Gras, so this place was packed, but the service was good and rather quick.

name: Duncan Steadman
text: Food was pretty good, overpriced for the quality. Would have left four stars, but our waitress did the very bare minimum. We've been in Vermont for almost two weeks, and  she was by far the worst server we have had. I'd expect her to work at a fast casual restaurant, not an upscale place. I won't be going back, with so many good restaurants in Burlington, Leunig's is just not worth the time or money.

name: Andrew Foley
text: What can I say, great drink selection! Try the Zero Gravity brew.

name: Tyler Antrim
text: My wife and I had our first date here. Always a good atmosphere.

name: Janet Winey
text: Well-known restaurant located on Church Street Marketplace.  The brunch menu was varied to appeal to diverse tastes.  The decor was a classic French bistro.  In summer, there is outdoor dining.  I was there in the fall and dined outdoors on a sunny October day, but in a plastic enclosure.  I enjoyed the food, location and atmosphere.

name: Philipp Foerster
text: Food was okay. Good but not delicious. The atmosphere is nice; the wait staff is kind but seems rushed.

name: Derek Rycewicz
text: Service is friendly and very fast for the quality of food, which is also very good. Brunch entrees were tasty, if a bit too salty and not particularly French. Coffee was mediocre. Overall pleased, but not amazed. We will probably be back to check out a few other menu options.

name: Barbara H
text: Great atmosphere, great food, cocktails, wine, local beers. What's not to like. Place is busy. We ended up eating at the bar and loved it. Great, attentive service. Our dinner choices Cavatappi Carbonara and the filet Mignon. It was our first time but based on the conversations around us they have many regulars.

name: Blade Sharp
text: Pretty good food and service.  Gets a star just for dining atmosphere.  Feels and looks a bit like a cafe in Europe.  The most professional waitstaff in Burlington and always nicely dressed as they should for an upscale restaurant. Nice place for sitting by window and people watching.

name: Tom Kimball
text: Leunig's is pretty good. I haven't had a horrible meal there, but nothing that has blown my mind either. For me, the prices are a bit high and are not quite offset by the atmosphere (which I do like).

name: Margi Swett
text: Wonderful portobello mushroom burger, great people watching, fun atmosphere

name: Edward Baciak
text: Always good.  French Onion soup is to die for.  Try the Key Lime Coconut Tart for dessert, yummy!

name: Martin Gold
text: Great location, great venue , terrific bar scene for a great night out. A bit pricey but worth it. Food is okay but not great.

name: Maxine Kravitz
text: A high quality french restaurant with a vermont twist. A lovely atmosphere, and with their petite shop outside on church st, this is a good place to stop for a quick bite or to sit down and relax for a while.

name: Joe Wehry
text: The deco-esque decor sets the stage for an expansive menu with a few vegetarian items. We enjoyed the kohlrabi fettuccini with vegetarian sausage. Be sure to take advantage of the early bird bistro dinner before 5:30pm.

name: Jess Peck
text: One of my favorite Burlington restaurants. Their steady menu is great, add in the seasonal specials and it's fantastic! Great atmosphere and seating, especially during the summer when they open up the huge windows and expand into Church Street.

name: TJ Jamyang
text: Good service.. good food.  Good location.

name: Heather Tackett
text: I had a great experience here. I ordered there salmon dish and it was perfect! We enjoyed the atmosphere of the Bistro and the music from the band that was playing. We will definitely be back again.

name: Douglas Wilfong
text: Always great food.  Lots of variety ... everything's delicious.  Excellent service and wine choices.

name: Noah Dion
text: Waited 25 minutes before finally being seated, only because another reservation hadn't shown up. Bartenders were friendly, waitstaff was as well. Hostess tried to seat my gf and I promptly but only after I had been standing while others sat, waiting for what seemed like forever. We should've gone somewhere else. The expense of the food did not outweigh the long and what seemed like gruesome wait. They need to be better about this on busy nights, they should turn people away with honesty about not being able to seat folks instead of making them stand. I'm a patient person btw. Just wasn't feeling the overall vibe

name: Ben
text: Cramped, busy...and yet...it works. The food and the atmosphere works for me. Always recommended as a plan or a accidental encounter.

name: Jamie Graham Gay
text:
Try a dumb thing: be allergic to wheat and dairy, then go to the nice French bistro in town. The cuisine of which is based almost entirely on those two foods.

Oops.

So with, I was not expecting to have a nice meal. I really wasn't expecting to have a great one, or to have a server who totally took my allergies in stride. On top of that, the ambiance out on Church Street was lovely.

Definitely recommended.

name: Deborah Blair
text: Leunig's Bistro is one of my favorite place to eat out in Vermont. It is more expensive than most of the Burlington restaurants - but it has always delivered a great meal for lunch or Dinner whenever I am entertaining friends. I have Doctor friends from Montreal who INSIST on eating here on their way into meetings or conferences in the states and on their way out - and they pride themselves on food. Over the last twenty years I have known that if I take out-of-state visitors out for a good meal - that I can depend on Leunig's  -  they have gourmet food - vegetarian and gluten free options - - some nights they have live music - - its a great place!!!

name: Carl Sedon
text: Beautiful place. Great food and drink. Comes so close to being in Paris.

name: C
text: Great church street stop for some appetizers and drinks.

name: FD G
text: I've been here a million times. And I will come one million more.

name: June Balachandran
text: I love this place so much for their duck confit poutine :)

name: Chatham Morell
text: Great food, great service and a pleasant experience

name: Kathryn Lemay
text: Leunigs is so good! There glazed corn beef hash is phenomenal.

name: Sally Leahey
text: Love the early bird delicious special!

name: Mr Anonymous
text: Great place to have a very nice dinner.  Located rite in the hart of church street and within walking distance to any amenity needed! Awesome food and great service!

name: Nicholas Champine
text: Exceptional service all around. Great place for lunch or dinner.

name: Jim Fitzpatrick
text:
I can guarantee you will not be disappointed!
This is the most consistent, well managed restaurant in Burlington.  The food is always excellent and the service is wonderful.

name: Ray Aley
text: Consistently delicious with outstanding service and ambiance.

name: F. Carl Mahoney
text: First rate atmosphere & cuisine.  A place to which you'll hope to return.

name: Ryk Edelstein
text: Usually a 10/10.. Most menu items are excellent unfortunately the kohlrabi "noodles" are a fail. IMHO.

resp.text: New dinner menu starts Monday, Feb 4th.  Noodles will be gone.

name: Al Getler
text: When we want a special night out, we choose Leunig's. When we want have visitors experience the best of Burlington, we choose Leunig's. The food is always well-prepared, the atmosphere is wonderful and the staff very attentive and friendly. We are lucky to have such a place in our community.

name: lester suarez
text: Best duck frites!

name: Robyn Latta
text: Love leunig's! Everything I've had there is delicious. It's a little expensive for dinner but so worth it. If you go for lunch you get almost everything available during dinner for a little less $. Highly recommend it.

name: Dave McGuriman
text: Excellent food our service was exceptional, theres a reason they are a burlington institution

name: Larae Sams
text: All I can say is mmmmmm.

name: Leo Lin
text: Food was amazing! Service was first class!

name: iain fletcher
text:
Tried the filet mignon excellent
They do need a few more wait staff service good but slow
Will go back again soon

name: Susan Sykas
text: Always great food and ambiance!

name: Jay Berger
text: Prices keep going up but the food quality doesn't match. Charging $4 for bread and funky butter doesn't fly in BTV.

name: Bob Nevins
text: Good food, great atmosphere.

name: Sharon Allen
text: Leunigs is a long time favourite and the food was good. My entrée,filet mignon had a few too many things going on but we'll certainly return

name: Valerie W
text: Off the hook fantastic, ask them to split an entrea and order an app. Everything is incredible.

name: Steve Burt
text: Annual cancer wine and food pairing benefit. Leunigs has been doing this for years. It's a great time.

name: William Eisner
text: We like to go for a nice pre-theater dinner. Very courteous staff and good food.

name: Jean Milano
text: Fantastic food and great service! Definitely recommend!

name: Mieneke Maher
text: They simply never disappoint. Food and ambiance all in one. Favorite place to go.

name: Kaleb Noble
text: The food was good, the waitstaff kind and attentive, and the atmosphere was great. I plan on going back.

name: Jon Marcinkiewicz
text: Very friendly.  Very good service.  A bit expensive.

name: John Dawson
text: Everything.  Always reliable, but always the same.  I love the Steak Frites for dinner and the Eggs Alaska for brunch.  Of course, the atmosphere and service are impeccable.  And if you get the chance, make sure you ask about their entertainment.  Trio Gusto on the deck is a fantastic evening you won't want to end.

name: Christian Adamczak
text: Very friendly staff and food was delicious just be prepared to spend upwards of $30 on a meal

name: Eddie Ling
text:
One of the worst dining experiences for myself and my partner and clearly for many other couples. We had a reservation for 8:45 but weren't seated until 9:05. We were sat in the upstairs area and it smelled awful, it was a heavy stench of boiling fat, body odor and cheese. Our appetizer came in ok time and was good. However our entrées took almost 80 minutes without and update or check in from the waitress save for a notice that it was being plated right before we were served. The filet mignon was okay, but accompanied by bland side vegetables and barely cooked fries. My partner's salmon was very bland and overcooked. There were 2 couples seated AFTER us yet they got there entrées before us, and there were at least 3 couples who were seated around the same time as us and got there food after us.

I understand that valentine's is a busy night, however leunigs was grossly under prepared. It is not the server's fault, however she did not once check in on us while waiting or offer any compensation for the long wait. The staff at leunigs needs to re-evaluate how to prepare and how to handle a busy night.

name: Mike
text: Bit expensive, but good food. It's been there since forever so that is a good sign that they know what they're doing. If you want French food, this is the place. Also- check out their late night menu (I believe after 9 or 10pm) it's only $20 per person for an app, entree, and dessert.

name: Rita
text: Amazing food and good wine selection. Outside seating in the summer is a must, as you can see everything going on around Church Street.

name: Joe Messingschlager
text: Excellent. Great food and ambiance. A authentic experience. Great service. You won't regret it.

name: Julie's bites
text: Very disappointed. Great location and atmosphere, but the food was not good. Out five dishes we ordered  we did not like any.  French onion soup was too salty.  Foie gras was the worst i ever had, I could only eat half (my favorite appetizer, first time in my life I did not finish it), duck slides were not good, I had to leave the duck uneaten, lamb had a strange after taste. All side dishes were flavorless. Food was presented in a sloppy way. Soup and appetizer arrived at the same time.  Positives? The staff was very pleasant, the atmosphere was great similar to a real French bistro, we sat next to an open window and I enjoyed the fresh air and the bustle of the street.  Food.... Not so much.

name: Amanda Poms
text: $$$ but worth it. Amazing food and one of my favorite places

name: Karen Johnson
text: Slider trio is delicious.

name: Kim Davis
text: Excellent food, atmosphere and service

name: Dana Basiliere
text: This is our goto eatery in downtown Burlington. We are never disappointed.

name: Albie Frye
text: Awesome food, awesome place....

name: Tammy Barney
text: Good food, attentive service, interesting cocktail menu.

name: Dr. Chris
text:
Had reservations for upstairs, but when I arrived the arrogant host said it was closed, and proceeded to sit us next to a window-less area where bugs freely came in and were a nuisance.

I ordered the burger medium, and after taking a bite I immediately spat it out as it was almost a tartar in the middle. The waitress offered to have it put back on the grill, but at that point my appetite was gone.

I refused to eat any more of it and still got charged for it. Two people, one meal half eaten for $136 was outrageous. I will never go back to this place - it exhibits the liberal lunacy that Vermont has sadly become. #LiberalismIsAMentalDisorder

name: Justin Anderson
text: Awesome food friendly staff

name: mike Mr. Bear
text: High priced, moderate food, quality

name: Rowan Livingston
text: Honestly, I can't possibly justify the prices here, considering the quality and portion sizes. I've eaten here several times and each time I've eaten it, the corned beef hash has been absolutely disgusting between the texture and the flavor. The Eggs Benedict it's alright, but I would not go here again. The only reason I've gone multiple times is because my mother and I used to have a pair of out-of-town guests who really liked it here. The main thing that's good about Leunigs is the wait staff. They're friendly and eager to serve customers. Even still, the prices make it far from worth it.

name: Dave Train
text: Good food, great service.

name: Wuji Fei
text: Good french food. I ordered the stew and it was pretty delicious. The portion is not big though, so I wasn't really full after I left.

name: Killian Hermann
text: The most pretentious service you could ask for, which may be forgivable if it were competent but is consistently lazy and dismissive. Overpriced tourist trap, inexplicably lauded in this town as some sort of landmark, it isn't. Sadly i am forced to dine here on occasion for business.

name: R Schuyler Watson
text: One of the top 10 places to eat in Burlington!

name: Pamela Jacobs
text: The food is good, but the last time I went, 3 of us ordered Steak Frites.  Everyone ordered a different doneness.  The waitress gave them to the wrong person.  You couldn't tell until you cut into it, it was too rare.  The person who was treating had the medium steak I ordered.  He didn't offer to switch.  I  didn't feel comfortable saying anything to the server.

name: david Devine
text: Great luncheon, service from Kelly, and Bob, gracious as ever.

name: lilsmomma1
text: Service, food, atmosphere, all exceptional

name: Lyndsey Irish
text: Delicious brunch but I'm disappointed to learn they stopped serving homefries with their brunch meals. They have Downtown Browns on the menu now, which is basically fancy homefries so you can still get them but have to pay extra.

name: Drew Emond
text: Delicious food, great atmosphere in and out!

name: Brennan Martin
text: Good food and a higher but not unreasonable price.  I have had slow service on multiple occasions.

name: B Horton

name: hieu mon chu
text:
Found this gem 5 years ago. The food is just as stellar today as it was when I first came. Though I kind of miss the old hole in the wall location.

The menu has all the classics of Vietnamese street food; rice dishes with grilled meats, rice noodle dishes, and of course, pho. Portions are a good value, with menu items over $12 generous enough for two when taken home and split.

The #33 is a great changeup to the pho, with both rice and egg noodles, shrimp, quail eggs, and a generous portion of tender, low fat pork. The #34 is the stir fried version,  also delicious.

The pho is the standout here. I have compared this pho side by side to the pho from another, more prominent Vietnamese restaurant.

Hands down, the Dang rules SUPREME!!

The key to pho is the extraction of gelatin from the beef marrow bones. After a triple wash (cold water on bones brought to a boil and dumped), the bones need 18+ hours on low simmer for full extraction. You can observe the gelatin content by letting the pho cool to 40 degrees F.

Cooling both of the samples of pho, the Dang pho is completely gelatinous, but solid enough to maintain the shape of the container when gently shaken.

Pho B was in a liquid form with no signs of gelatin forming. Pho B was also heavy on the aromatics normally used (star anise, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, and coriander seeds).

Gelatin in the broth is what gives richness to the liquid, delivering an incomparable mouth feel. There is no shortcut to this.  Neither msg, salt, nor aromatics can come close to replicating this.

Attempting to accelerate the process with high heat will destroy the clarity of the broth. A gentle simmer is critical.

Pho broth, at its essence,  is a classic french broth, consomme like, but without simmering with a raft to clarify the liquid.

The chef is a master of this craft.

Thank you chefs for keeping our culture alive!!!

Not only did the new counter girl not know what she was doing, she didn't wash her hands or use gloves after handling money, and the phone... and my food.

I got 2 slices around 4pm. and by 9pm I was in agony, stomachache kept me up all night, It's now been 20 hours and I'm still in pain, unable to eat anything, or go outside. this is unacceptable.

Unfortunately you've lost a customer. A place making me sick once can happen, but 3 times in the past 2 months? I'm out.

text: I stopped here with my wife and 1 year old on a Saturday evening. We didn't have reservations so we had to eat in the barroom which was fine with us. They were very accommodating with a highchair for our little guy. The craft beer selection was pretty good. The food was fantastic and they brought out warm breed and sweet butter that was to die for. The only real problem was the late service. From the time we arrived till we received our meals was over an hour. This was unacceptable. We never received a reason why. Neighbors ordered and received theirs way before us. Not sure if our waiter just never put in our order or the kitchen screwed up but they never even apologized for the late meal. They were lucky our toddler was well behaved while waiting over an hour. I would love to go back but not sure if it will happen.

name: Jeffrey Currier
text:
Windsor Station is featured in an original train station, with appropriate decor. It has smallish menu, leaning toward Italian. To night, my first visit, I had dinner with friends. I had a bowl of spaghetti and meatballs balls, which underwhelmed me. The sauce was not a knockout. Chefs who make meatballs need to travel to Italy, or at least Boston's North End for a bench mark. I will admit my blended cocktail, was a winner! Our waitress was also very professional, albeit for lack of filling our water. (Another nit pick of mine.). I dunno. I guess I'd try it again, it had a charming look.

*Post script...After what was a snarky remark from the owner, about my review, I will NOT return to Windsor Station. When I take my good time to mention both good and not so good points about an establishment, it's to help them work to make a truly fine dining experience.  If the chef wants to taste a good sauce and meatball, try the Pizza Stone in Chester, Vermont. Otherwise, he can take their ego and ignorance and serve it on a cracker. Just not my cracker.

resp.text: the north end in Boston is hilariously far from Italian , tourist trap

The former manager and her staff at the Williston Rd location in South Burlington, Vermont, as of the end October were great. I had visited many times. Friendly, helpful, and professional.
I went in last week, and all of the old crew were gone. It was obvious that there had been a change of guard. One guy was back in the kitchen barking at the crew. The person  on the register was abrupt and rude. He acted angry, as if he was doing me a favor even waiting on me.  After I asked him several times, and he pretended not to hear, he admitted to be being the new owner. It must just be a money laundering operation, because they DEFINITELY don't want to wait on customers. I  won't go back.
Al's French Fry's  ( that's their spelling, not mine) is 100 yards away. Much better quality, hand cut fries, everything cooked to order fantastic help.  And now inside dining ! I only went to McDonald's because I liked their coffee, anyhow.

name: Andrew Swift
text: A franchise of the famous Chicago eatery, this location has nice, friendly staff and the service is quick and attentive. On weekends, especially game days, expect a crowd. The atmosphere is perfect for game day, so consider. Parking is plentiful. The food is above average, and the menu changes, although pizza is the draw. Highly recommended!

name: Kyle Clark
text: Very good experience! Food very good! Burger cooked perfectly! Waitress was super! Very friendly. Made sure we had everything we needed, put our appetizer right in before she took our entree. name: Bob Harris
text: Absolutely love pizzeria Uno.  Some love New York style - some like Detroit style.  This is a good representation of deep dish Chicago style. The pies are small but very dense, delicious, and desirable.   If you haven't tried the Classic it's wonderful.  Weight watchers and vegans be warned 😊.  Meant to be eaten with a fork....

name: Robert Fillioe
text: Weather it it's comfort food or a very nice steak dinner you can find it all here. Today was very hot so we chose the lighter fare. Goat cheese and berry salad for my wife and a wedge salad for me. Yummy!  Add a cold beverage and you have a nutritious meal that is both satisfying and refreshing. Then add Violette, our waitress and your dining experience is complete. Fair prices, good service and bountiful choices make this the place to go. You won't be disappointed.

text: I have never had UNO's before, but I was definitely impressed with the staff and how nice they were.  Michael did a great job on his first day!  And the food was excellent.

name: Tracey Morrow
text: We had been there before, but not for quite some time. This day we'd been car shopping in the area and decided to grab a very late lunch before jumping on the interstate. We were seated in the bar area, which was chilly and very loud--people yelling back and forth (including the bartender). Neither of us felt like having pizza, which-in their defense-was probably our biggest mistake, since it is a pizza place! I had a chicken parmigiana pizzanini, which I pictured as a chicken parm sandwich on a thin crust sort of thing from the description. There was hardly any chicken (or cheese, for that matter) involved, the crust was dry and hard, and the fries served on the side were cold. My hubby had a burger, which he said was okay, but greasy, and his fries were also cold. Unfortunately, we never saw our server until we were ready to leave, so didn't have an opportunity to ask for warm fries. Overall, not a good experience.

resp.text:
Tracey, I am very sorry we failed to deliver a great dining experience today. No excuses. Please reach out to me at comments@unos.com. Allow me to extend a personal apology and make amends.
Amanda S.

name: Michel Loiselle
text: A favorite place for lunch or dinner. I got hooked years ago when they used to offer New Orleans Fettuccini, my all time favorite dish anywhere! Since they don't have that anymore, I opt for the Snakebite Pasta. Spicy and good, but not even close to being the New Orleans dish! Please bring it back!

text: Solid food, good atmosphere, friendly and efficient waitstaff. Prices are reasonable.

text: There was a ton of open tables and there was a 25 min wait and no bartender with a wait at the bar as well! Tons of open tables and tons of room at the bar. We left after waiting 10 minutes. Used to be a good spot.

resp.text:
Thank you for sharing this experience with us. I am sorry it happened. Your feedback will be shared with our Regional Team to ensure a better experience for all of our guests. I hope you will return in the near future and give us the opportunity to redeem ourselves.
Amanda S.

name: Taylor Boomhover
text: It took awhile to be seated when we could see many tables empty and we were told 10 mins. It was 4 of us and our 16 month old and they seated us in the table that had been empty since we got there. Our waiter took awhile to come over. I never got my side salad which came with my meal. My ziti had been sitting under the heat lamp so long most of the noodles were hard and my husbands chicken parm sandwich wasnt good as well. It took almost our whole meal to get refills and our friends were never even offered refills on alcoholic beverages. I still tipped 20% because it was a holiday and who knows what kind of day hes had. But I expected better food for the prices. Highly do not reccomend....we were suppose to eat at the olive garden but the wait was an hour.

resp.text:
Taylor, I am sorry for this disappointing visit to UNO. Please reach out to me at comments@unos.com. Allow me to extend a personal apology and have the opportunity to convince you to give us another try. I promise we are better than this visit.
Amanda S.

name: Eric LaMontagne
text:
Disclaimer - this is a reflection on the Jiffy Lube corporation. The staff experience I had there today was exemplary. They were quick, polite, and accommodating. I admit to being inflamed when I saw it was going to be $106 for a dang oil change (full synthetic), but it's important to note that these hard working local folks are not the ones setting the prices and are not to be blamed for Jiffy Lube's repulsive corporate culture.

And repulsive it is. As a corporation, Jiffy Lube represents the worst of the worst in corporate greed and piracy. They force you to pay for services you don't need. Want your oil changed? Guess what, you have to pay to have them to check your transfer case, differentials, and radiator as well. Have a 4x4 or AWD vehicle? There is an undisclosed up-charge for that. Yes, despite the fact that a 2wd and 4wd vehicle can have the EXACT SAME ENGINE, it's more to get the 4wd's oil change done. Why? "Because of the extra drive axle" and the associated fluids they have to check. Don't want them to check it? Tough luck. You have no choice. Just washed and vacuumed your car? You have to pay them to do it anyway. IF ALL YOU WANT IS AN OIL CHANGE, DON'T USE JIFFY LUBE. That said, if you want the comfort of knowing everything has been checked (which, of course, is a great opportunity for them to up-sell you), then by all means give them a go. But being force-fed these unwanted services and not being given the choice is a miserable way to conduct business.

resp.text: Eric, we want you to know your concerns are taken to heart, and we very much hope you will help us put you in touch with the appropriate member of our leadership team by sending your best availability, contact number, and this review link for reference to guest.relations@jiffyworld.com. name: Ben Roberts TV
text: Unfortunately I'm unable to give a 5 star review to the Ronald McDonald House in Burlington,  VT.  My newborn niece is a patient at the UVM Medical Center in critical care.  My nieces mother lives nearly two hours from the UVM Medical Center.  To be able to stay at the Ronald McDonald House a referral is required from the UVM social worker assigned to the patient.  The social worker assigned won't do a referral and has given the mother of the baby two options.   Option 1 to commute daily, which would be a nearly 4 hour round trip commute.  Option 2 being to rent a motel room.  Neither of these options are feasible.   A woman that recently gave birth and her body is still healing isn't going to drive a nearly 4 hour commute daily.   Since the mother is on unpaid maternity leave from her job she can't financially afford to rent a motel room.  Since my family member is being denied to stay at the Ronald McDonald House during this difficult time, I can't give their establishment a good review at this time.

resp.text: Our process for admission starts with the referral from the hospital. For a variety of safety, security and procedural reasons we are only introduced to our families once that referral is received from the hospital. We work with the social work department at the Children's Hospital on a daily basis and they understand our requirements for referrals. Given restrictions due to Covid-19 at that time, there is a chance the referring social worker knew our limitations.

name: Blithe Milks
text:
It doesn't hurt that it's a beautiful day. Which also means it was packed in the parking lot and the building. The man driving the tractor asked what we were looking for and gave great recommendations for where to find different species. Once among the trees, we hardly saw any other people.
The petting zoo had a lot of people. Most of them short. Between the toddlers and the poop, watch your feet. The feed vending machines are stingy. Not a fun time for your average vegan: lots of caged animals and babies without access to moms. Don't think too hard.
Buy the doughnuts when you can! Do not wait until later! They will sell out. Amazing pumpkins and baked goods.
Friendly helpful staff. Clean rustic bathrooms. Didn't see changing tables.
Go on a beautiful day and wear sturdy shoes.

resp.text: Blithe, Thank you for your thoughtful review! We appreciate you!
